Name: steering_reliability_collapse
Title: Controlled but Unrepresentable: Does Interpretable-Feature Steering Push Scientific Generative Models Into Their Own Confidence Blind Spots?
Short Hypothesis: Steering interpretable features to control a target property silently drags generation into regions of sequence/molecule space where the model's OWN representation becomes unreliable (embedding-quality collapses toward random-like), so the apparent property gain is untrustworthy exactly where steering is strongest. We hypothesize a cheap, intervention-free internal representation-reliability score falls monotonically with steering strength, predicts when the claimed property is real vs illusory, and can gate steering to keep only trustworthy controlled designs—an axis that output-side property predictors and validity checks completely miss.
Related Work: Two threads meet for the first time. (1) SAE/neuron steering of scientific generative models (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; FoldSAE 2025; Automated Neuron Labelling 2025; Steering PLMs/ASPO 2025; ProtoMech 2026; antibody SAE 2025) all report property GAIN from steering and evaluate success via property predictors; none asks whether steering pushes outputs into regions where the model can no longer reliably represent them. (2) Representation-reliability work—'Quantifying Uncertainty in Protein Representations Across Models and Tasks' (2025) shows pLM embeddings for undersampled sequences become vector-indistinguishable from random, and 'Quantifying Feature Space Universality' plus data-saturation studies show embedding quality tracks training coverage—but this is studied only for NATURAL inputs, never as a CONSEQUENCE of steering, and never linked to the trustworthiness of controlled designs. No prior work (a) shows steering induces representation-reliability collapse, (b) demonstrates that property predictors and validity checks fail to detect this while an internal reliability score does, or (c) uses reliability to gate steering. This is distinct from my prior proposals on memorization-attractors (about contractive attractors resisting steering), validity-foresight (about invalid finished objects), and infeasible-spec frustration (about contradictory constraints): here the finished object can be perfectly valid and hit the property predictor, yet sit in a representational blind spot that makes the control claim untrustworthy.
Abstract: Interpretable-feature steering is the dominant tool for controllable design of proteins and molecules, and it is judged almost entirely by whether a target-property predictor says the property increased. We surface a hidden failure mode: the very act of steering can push generation into regions where the model's own internal representation becomes unreliable—its embeddings drift toward random-like, low-information vectors—so the property 'gain' is measured on objects the model can no longer faithfully represent. Because the objects still look valid (they fold, they parse) and still satisfy an external predictor, standard evaluations miss this entirely. We hypothesize that a cheap, intervention-free representation-reliability score (embedding self-consistency / distance-to-random / feature-activation coherence) declines monotonically with steering strength, that it predicts per-generation whether the claimed property is real (agrees with a held-out physics oracle) versus illusory, and that gating steering by this score recovers a trustworthy control-validity-reliability frontier. Using ESM-2 protein language models and a SMILES chemical language model with sparse autoencoders, we (1) demonstrate reliability collapse as a function of steering strength and target property; (2) show that output-side property predictors and validity checks fail to flag it while the internal reliability score succeeds; (3) causally test whether reliability collapse is what makes the property claim untrustworthy by comparing predictor-property against an independent oracle stratified by reliability; and (4) deploy a reliability-gated steering controller that keeps only trustworthy designs. Results would add representational reliability as a necessary, currently-ignored axis for controllable scientific design.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: ESM-2 at 150M and 650M parameters and a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~90M), base weights frozen. SAEs: TopK (k=32, dictionary 16384) and Matryoshka on the mid-layer (60% depth) residual stream, trained on 200M activations, seeds {0,1}, FVU reported. Feature bank of 20-40 property-linked features (probe AUROC>=0.8 on 2,000 held-out natural objects): proteins -- alpha-helix/beta-sheet fraction, GRAVY, molecular weight, a thermostability proxy head, motifs; molecules -- logP, QED, ring/aromatic counts, functional groups. Property predictors used the way the steering literature uses them (DSSP/ESMFold, biopython, fine-tuned heads, RDKit/SMARTS). Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT>=0.6 + pseudo-perplexity within 1.5x baseline (proteins); RDKit-validity + SA<=6 (molecules). Steering budget in normalized activation-norm units; SAE-feature, difference-of-means, and norm-matched random-direction interventions. REPRESENTATION-RELIABILITY SCORE (intervention-free), combining: (a) distance-to-random -- Mahalanobis/cosine gap between the object's embedding and the distribution of embeddings of shuffled/random sequences; (b) embedding self-consistency under small input perturbations (masking/dropout); (c) SAE-feature coherence (co-firing consistency vs natural objects); validated on natural held-out objects to track known coverage/neighbor-density signals before any steering use.

Experiment 1 (H1 -- Steering pushes representations toward unreliable regions; H2 -- monotone collapse with strength). Tests that the reliability score declines monotonically with steering strength, often before validity or property-predictor gain break down. Data/systems: for each feature/property, sweep steering strength {0...1.0 budget units}; at each level generate 500 objects and record property-predictor gain, validity, and reliability score; compare SAE-feature, difference-of-means, and random-direction steering. Decisive metric (primary): slope of reliability vs steering strength (mixed-effects), and the COLLAPSE-BEFORE-VALIDITY GAP = steering strength at which reliability crosses the natural-object 5th-percentile threshold minus the strength at which validity fails. Convincing positive: reliability slope significantly negative and monotone (Spearman rho <= -0.7 vs strength) with a positive collapse-before-validity gap >= 0.2 budget units in the majority of properties. Decision band: gap in [0, 0.2) budget units means reliability and validity collapse together -- the phenomenon exists but offers little early-warning headroom; reported as such. Negative: non-monotone or flat reliability (rho > -0.3), or a negative gap (validity fails first), refutes H1/H2 -- reliability collapse is not a distinct pre-validity failure mode, a clean negative result.

Experiment 2 (H3 -- Low reliability marks illusory property gains). Tests that the property "gain" is real when reliability is high and illusory when low, adjudicated by an independent oracle. Data/systems: for a subset of steered generations, score the target property with an INDEPENDENT oracle not used in steering (proteins: FoldX/Rosetta-style stability or a distinct structure metric; molecules: a second empirical logP model or docking); stratify by reliability quartile. Decisive metric (primary): predictor-vs-oracle agreement on the target property per reliability quartile (correlation or concordance). Convincing positive: agreement in the top reliability quartile exceeds the bottom quartile by >= 0.3 (correlation units), CI excludes 0 -- gains are trustworthy only when reliable. Decision band: quartile gap in [0.1, 0.3) means reliability weakly tracks trustworthiness -- reported as a soft signal, not a gate. Negative: gap <= 0.1 (predictor-oracle agreement independent of reliability) means the reliability score does not distinguish real from illusory gains, refuting H3 even if collapse (H1/H2) occurs.

Experiment 3 (H4 -- Output-side signals miss it; the internal score catches it). Tests that validity and property-predictor confidence are near-chance at flagging untrustworthy control while the internal reliability score succeeds. Data/systems: predict "low predictor-oracle agreement" (from Experiment 2) using the internal reliability score vs output-side baselines -- the predictor's own confidence, pseudo-perplexity, ESMFold pLDDT / RDKit-validity, and a black-box raw-activation reliability probe. Decisive metric: AUROC and calibration ECE for flagging untrustworthy generations. Convincing positive: reliability-score AUROC >= 0.80 with ECE<=0.10 while output-side validity/property-confidence stay in [0.45, 0.60] (near chance), the SAE score adding which-features-decohere interpretability. Decision band: reliability-score AUROC in [0.65, 0.80), or its edge over the black-box probe in [0.03, 0.10) AUROC, means the internal signal works but its advantage over cheaper signals is marginal -- the interpretability payoff is then the contribution. Negative: output-side signals already reach AUROC>=0.70, or the reliability score fails to beat them, means H4's "completely miss" claim is refuted.

Experiment 4 (H4 -- Reliability-gated steering keeps only trustworthy designs). Tests that gating steering by the reliability score yields a better trustworthy-yield-per-compute frontier than ungated or validity-only gating. Data/systems: a controller that rejects/down-weights steering driving reliability below the natural-object threshold, vs ungated steering and validity-only gating, over the same property battery. Decisive metric (primary): fraction of generations simultaneously oracle-property-satisfying, valid, and reliable (trustworthy yield), and trustworthy-yield-per-unit-compute; secondary: diversity/novelty retention and compute saved by not validating untrustworthy designs. Convincing positive: reliability-gating raises trustworthy yield by >= 20% relative to validity-only gating at equal or lower compute, without collapsing diversity (novelty retained within 10% of ungated). Decision band: improvement in [5%, 20%) is a modest, reported gain; improvement that comes only with a large diversity loss (>10%) is reported as a trade, not a free lunch. Negative: reliability-gating gives <= 5% trustworthy-yield improvement over validity-only gating, meaning the reliability axis adds no practical control value beyond existing checks.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The independent oracle (FoldX/Rosetta/second logP model/docking) is itself an in-silico proxy; the trustworthiness claim rests on DISAGREEMENT between two independent in-silico signals stratified by reliability, not wet-lab truth—stated explicitly. 2) The reliability score could merely correlate with off-distribution-ness rather than causing untrustworthy property claims; we mitigate by (a) validating it on natural objects with known coverage and (b) the reliability-stratified oracle test that ties low reliability to predictor failure, and by random-direction controls. 3) An internal SAE-based reliability score might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; even so, interpretability (naming which features decohere) and the frontier/compute gains are the contribution and are reported honestly. 4) Reliability collapse might be trivially entangled with validity collapse; the core test specifically isolates the regime where objects remain valid and predictor-satisfying yet unreliable, and reports the gap—if no such gap exists, that is itself a clean, publishable negative result. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound both steering and reliability; controlled via multiple SAE variants, layers, and difference-of-means baselines. 6) In-silico property/validity evaluators are proxies; claims concern model-internal representational trustworthiness of controlled designs, not experimental function.

Relative to the closest prior work on SAE steering, the delta is not a new steering method but a new failure mode and diagnostic. Name: provenance_shortcut_steering
Title: Designing the Database, Not the Molecule: Do Interpretable Features Reveal That Steered Scientific Generators Chase Dataset Provenance Instead of Physics?
Short Hypothesis: When we steer a protein/molecule generative model toward a desired PHYSICAL property (e.g., high thermostability), the model frequently satisfies the target by moving along interpretable features that encode DATASET PROVENANCE (source organism, protein family, structural-database membership, assay batch) rather than the underlying physics. The apparent property gain is a shortcut: it reproduces the provenance signature correlated with the property in the training data, and interpretable features expose this so we can detect it and steer against it.
Related Work: Prior pLM-SAE work (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; 'From Mechanistic Interpretability to Mechanistic Biology' 2025; functional-annotation SAE work 2025) repeatedly finds that pLMs represent proteins via a mix of generic biophysical features AND strong 'family-specific'/organism-specific features, and steering studies add a target property by moving along whatever feature correlates with it. Separately, data-leakage and batch-effect work ('Beware of Data Leakage from Protein LLM Pretraining' 2024; thermostability leakage; batch-effect correction literature) shows downstream property predictors are inflated by provenance confounds. Recent critical work ('Dead Salmons of AI Interpretability' 2025; 'Automated Interpretability Metrics Do Not Distinguish Trained and Random Transformers' 2025; single-cell FM interpretability 2026 finding attention captures co-expression not causal signal) warns that interpretable-looking signals may be spurious. NO prior work connects these: no one asks whether interpretable-feature STEERING for design achieves property gains by exploiting provenance-artifact features rather than causal physics, quantifies how often this happens, or uses interpretability to disentangle a provenance-shortcut direction from a physics direction. This is distinct from all my prior proposals (compositionality, off-mode reach, steerability prediction, leakage, reliability collapse), which all assumed the property gain, when achieved, is legitimate.
Abstract: Steering interpretable features has become the standard way to make protein and molecule generators produce objects with a desired physical property, and success is judged by a property predictor. We surface a hidden behavioral phenomenon: because training corpora are riddled with provenance confounds (a property co-occurs with a source organism, a protein family, or a structural-database subset), a generator can satisfy a physical-property target by shifting the DATASET PROVENANCE of its output rather than its physics—a shortcut that inflates the predictor but need not reflect real physical mechanism. We use interpretability to expose this. Training sparse autoencoders on ESM-2 (proteins) and a SMILES chemical LM, we identify two kinds of feature directions per target property: physics-aligned directions (correlated with the property after controlling for provenance) and provenance-aligned directions (correlated with source organism/family/database membership). We test three claims: (1) standard property-steering moves substantially along provenance features, and its gain shrinks or vanishes when scored by a provenance-controlled oracle; (2) the fraction of the achieved property gain attributable to provenance predicts a designer-relevant failure—steered designs cluster tightly with a training-data provenance group and lose novelty/mechanistic diversity; and (3) explicitly orthogonalizing the steering direction against provenance features (provenance-invariant steering) preserves genuine property gain while restoring novelty and provenance-controlled predictor agreement. We report a provenance-shortcut score, its correlation with spurious gains, and a simple debiasing recipe. Results recast interpretable features as an audit that separates designing-the-molecule from designing-the-database.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: ESM-2 at 150M and 650M parameters (proteins) and a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~90M), base weights frozen. SAEs: TopK (k=32, dictionary 16384) and Matryoshka on the mid-layer (60% depth) residual stream, trained on 200M activations, seeds {0,1}, FVU reported. Target PHYSICAL properties with cheap evaluators: proteins -- thermostability proxy (fine-tuned head), GRAVY, secondary-structure fraction (DSSP on ESMFold); molecules -- logP, a solubility proxy, QED. PROVENANCE labels per training object: proteins -- source organism/taxon, Pfam family, PDB/CATH structural-database membership; molecules -- source assay/dataset (ChEMBL target/document id), scaffold class. Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT>=0.6 + pseudo-perplexity within 1.5x baseline (proteins); RDKit-validity + SA<=6 (molecules). Steering budget in normalized activation-norm units; SAE-feature, difference-of-means, and norm-matched random-direction interventions. ~8 property x domain settings; 500 generations per condition.

Experiment 1 (H1 -- Features split into physics-aligned vs provenance-aligned, and standard steering rides provenance). Tests that standard property steering moves substantially along provenance-encoding features. Data: per SAE feature compute correlation with the target property and mutual information with provenance labels over 2,000 held-out natural objects; partition into provenance-aligned (high provenance MI), physics-aligned (property correlation surviving provenance stratification / partial correlation), and mixed. Systems compared: standard steering via best-property-correlated SAE feature and difference-of-means direction vs a norm-matched random direction; decompose the steering displacement onto provenance vs physics feature subspaces. Decisive metric (primary): PROVENANCE-SUBSPACE DISPLACEMENT FRACTION = share of the steering displacement lying in the provenance subspace. Convincing positive: displacement fraction >= 0.4 (median over settings) and clearly above the random-direction control's incidental overlap. Decision band: fraction in [0.2, 0.4) means steering partially rides provenance -- reported as a contributing, not dominant, shortcut. Negative: fraction < 0.2 (steering stays in the physics subspace) refutes H1 for that property -- a valuable positive result that steering targets physics, not database artifacts.

Experiment 2 (H2 -- The gain is spurious: it shrinks under a provenance-controlled oracle). Tests that the property gain scored by a provenance-decorrelated oracle is much smaller than by the naive predictor. Data/systems: for each steered generation, score property gain by (i) the naive predictor and (ii) a PROVENANCE-CONTROLLED oracle -- a predictor trained on a provenance-balanced/decorrelated split and/or an independent physics evaluator (FoldX/Rosetta-style stability; a second empirical logP model) that ignores provenance. Decisive metric (primary): SPURIOUS GAIN = naive-minus-controlled property-gain gap, as a fraction of the naive gain. Convincing positive: spurious gain >= 40% of naive gain (median, CI excludes 0) and correlated with the provenance-displacement fraction from Experiment 1 (Spearman rho>=0.5). Decision band: spurious gain in [15%, 40%) means part of the gain is real physics -- reported as a partial shortcut. Negative: spurious gain < 15% (controlled oracle largely confirms the naive gain) refutes H2 -- the gain reflects physics, and the shortcut account is withdrawn for that property.

Experiment 3 (H2/H3 -- The shortcut predicts designer-relevant failure). Tests that high-shortcut steering yields provenance-collapsed, low-novelty designs. Data/systems: per steered generation compute a provenance-shortcut score (share of gain attributable to provenance movement) and measure provenance clustering (collapse toward one organism/family/scaffold group in embedding space), novelty (identity/Tanimoto to nearest training object), and set diversity; regress these on the shortcut score. Decisive metric: Spearman rho / R^2 between shortcut score and provenance-collapse and novelty-loss. Convincing positive: rho >= 0.5 (CI excludes 0) for both collapse and novelty-loss -- the shortcut is a usable predictor of degenerate design. Decision band: rho in [0.3, 0.5) is a weak predictor -- reported with its error. Negative: rho <= 0.3 means the shortcut score does not forecast design degeneration, so its practical value is limited even if H1/H2 hold.

Experiment 4 (H3 -- Provenance-invariant steering fixes it; positive control validates the pipeline). Tests that orthogonalizing the steering direction against provenance features preserves genuine (controlled-oracle) gain while restoring novelty and reducing collapse, and that the whole detection/fix pipeline recovers a known planted shortcut. Data/systems: (a) construct a debiased direction by projecting the property direction off the provenance subspace (Gram-Schmidt), compare provenance-invariant vs standard steering at matched displacement on controlled-oracle gain, provenance-collapse, novelty, validity; (b) POSITIVE CONTROL -- relabel a subset so a property artificially co-occurs with a tag, confirm the pipeline recovers the planted shortcut and the fix removes it. Decisive metrics: change in controlled-oracle gain and in novelty/collapse from invariant vs standard steering; and planted-shortcut recovery rate in the positive control. Convincing positive: invariant steering retains >= 80% of the controlled-oracle gain while cutting provenance-collapse by >= 30% and restoring novelty toward the unsteered baseline, AND the positive control recovers the planted shortcut (detection AUROC>=0.9) with the fix removing it. Decision band: controlled-gain retention in [60%, 80%) or collapse reduction in [10%, 30%) means the fix trades some genuine signal for debiasing -- reported as a quantified trade. Negative: invariant steering destroys controlled-oracle gain (retention < 60%) means physics and provenance are inseparable for that property (reported per property), or a failed positive control invalidates the pipeline and is reported before any real-data claim.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Provenance-controlled oracles and physics evaluators (FoldX/Rosetta, second logP model) are in-silico proxies; the core claim rests on DISAGREEMENT between a naive predictor and a provenance-decorrelated one, plus displacement into a provenance feature subspace—stated explicitly, not as wet-lab truth. 2) Physics and provenance may be irreducibly entangled for some properties (family IS the mechanism); we handle this by reporting the entanglement per property and restricting strong claims to properties where a provenance-orthogonal physics direction demonstrably exists (validated by the controlled oracle). 3) The debiasing fix could remove genuine signal if physics and provenance share a subspace; we quantify the tradeoff via the controlled oracle rather than assume a free lunch. 4) SAE quality/layer choice could produce spurious 'provenance features'; controlled with multiple SAE variants, difference-of-means baselines, random-direction controls, and the synthetic positive control (experiment 6). 5) If standard steering turns out NOT to ride provenance (gains survive the controlled oracle), that is a valuable positive result establishing that interpretable-feature steering targets physics, not database artifacts. 6) In-silico property/validity metrics limit conclusions to model-internal design behavior, not experimental function.

novelty.reasoning: Core claims: (1) interpretable steering for protein/molecule generation can achieve target-property gains by following dataset provenance shortcuts rather than causal physical structure; (2) SAE-interpretable features can be partitioned into provenance-aligned vs physics-aligned directions and used to audit steering behavior; (3) the gap between naive predictor gains and provenance-controlled oracle gains quantifies shortcut exploitation; (4) provenance-orthogonalized steering can reduce shortcuting while preserving real gains; (5) a planted-shortcut positive control can validate the detection pipeline. From the proposal and search summary, the closest prior work is the family of protein-property leakage/batch-effect papers plus interpretable feature steering and critical-interpretability critiques. The actual delta is not just applying leakage concerns to generation, but reframing interpretability-based steering as a provenance-audit problem and proposing a debiasing intervention. That is meaningfully non-trivial and not an obvious one-line extension, though it still studies known confounds and known steering machinery rather than introducing a wholly new modeling paradigm.

Name: steering_sideeffect_law
Title: The Conservation of Trouble: Are Off-Target Property Drifts of Interpretable-Feature Steering Lawful and Predictable in Scientific Generative Models?
Short Hypothesis: When an interpretable feature is steered to control one property of a generated protein or molecule, it induces off-target drift in OTHER, structurally-verifiable properties that is not random noise but LAWFUL: the drift vector across all properties is predicted, before any generation, by a fixed feature-specific 'side-effect signature' derived from the geometry of the SAE dictionary. This lets practitioners forecast and pre-empt collateral damage, choosing minimal-side-effect features and orthogonalized directions to hit a target property while holding others fixed.
Related Work: Text-LLM steering studies extensively document off-target side effects and entanglement: SAE-Targeted Steering (Chalnev et al. 2024) minimizes side effects using SAE-measured effect vectors; Rogue Scalpel (2025), Steering Externalities (2026), SteeringSafety (2025), Steering Refusal with SAEs (2024), and Mind the Performance Gap (2026) all show steering degrades unrelated capabilities or safety in a method/model-dependent way. Crucially, all of these (a) operate in TEXT LLMs where the off-target 'property' is a fuzzy behavior or benchmark score, and (b) treat side effects as a nuisance to be measured post hoc or empirically minimized. Scientific-model steering work (InterPLM 2024, ProtSAE 2025, chemistry-LM SAEs) reports only ON-target property gains and evaluates validity as a side constraint, never characterizing structured off-target property drift. No prior work (i) transfers the off-target-drift phenomenon to scientific generative models where every off-target property (helix content, charge, logP, ring count, motif presence) is an OBJECTIVELY VERIFIABLE structural fact, (ii) tests whether the drift is LAWFUL and predictable a priori from a fixed feature side-effect signature rather than needing per-target measurement, or (iii) turns that law into a pre-flight side-effect forecaster and a minimal-collateral feature/direction selector. This distinguishes it from my prior compositionality proposal (which co-steers several INTENDED targets) by studying UNINTENDED drift on non-targeted properties and its a-priori predictability.
Abstract: Steering interpretable features to control a target property of a generated protein or molecule is the standard controllable-design paradigm, and it is judged almost entirely by whether the target property moves. In text language models, steering is known to cause unintended off-target effects, but there the 'off-target property' is a fuzzy behavior and the effect is treated as a post-hoc nuisance. We transfer this phenomenon to scientific generative models, where every off-target property is an objectively verifiable structural fact, and ask a sharper question: is the collateral drift lawful and predictable BEFORE any generation? We hypothesize that each interpretable feature carries a fixed 'side-effect signature'—the direction in property space it perturbs—computable from the SAE dictionary geometry (via decoder-direction overlaps and a per-feature property-Jacobian), so that steering toward property A produces a forecastable drift vector across properties B, C, D that no output-side check anticipates. Using ESM-2 protein language models and a SMILES chemical language model with sparse autoencoders, we (1) demonstrate that single-target steering induces substantial, structured off-target property drift measured by hard oracles (DSSP/ESMFold, biopython, RDKit/SMARTS); (2) test whether an intervention-free side-effect signature predicts each feature's actual drift vector across steering strengths (a 'steering side-effect law'); (3) validate the signature as a pre-flight forecaster that ranks features by expected collateral damage; and (4) deploy a minimal-collateral controller—selecting low-side-effect features or orthogonalizing the steering direction against high-drift property axes—to hit the target while holding others fixed, tracing a target-gain-versus-collateral frontier. Results would recast off-target drift from an unpredictable hazard into a forecastable, controllable design quantity.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: ESM-2 at 150M and 650M parameters and a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~90M), base weights frozen. SAEs: TopK (k=32, dictionary 16384) and Matryoshka on the mid-layer (60% depth) residual stream, trained on 200M activations, seeds {0,1}, FVU reported. Property battery, each with a cheap HARD oracle so drift is objective: proteins -- alpha-helix fraction, beta-sheet fraction, GRAVY, net charge, molecular weight, motif presence (HMMER/regex); molecules -- logP, QED, ring/aromatic-ring count, molecular weight, TPSA, functional-group SMARTS. Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT>=0.6 + pseudo-perplexity within 1.5x baseline (proteins); RDKit-validity + SA<=6 (molecules). Feature bank: ~30-50 property-linked target features per domain (probe AUROC>=0.8 on 2,000 held-out natural objects) plus difference-of-means directions. Steering budget in normalized activation-norm units; norm-matched random-direction controls throughout; 500 generations per feature x strength level.

Experiment 1 (H1 -- Single-target steering induces structured, non-random off-target drift). Tests that steering one property drifts other properties in a consistent, non-noise direction. Data/systems: for each target feature, sweep steering strength {0.1...1.0}; at each level measure the FULL property vector; the off-target drift vector = change in every non-target property; compare against a norm-matched random direction. Decisive metrics: (a) collateral magnitude = off-target drift norm relative to on-target gain; (b) DIRECTION CONSISTENCY = mean cosine of the drift vector across seeds and adjacent strengths; (c) correlation of output-side checks (validity/pseudo-perplexity/RDKit-validity) with true off-target drift. Convincing positive: direction consistency >= 0.7 (drift is a stable signature, well above the random-direction control's ~0) AND output-side-vs-drift correlation in [-0.2, 0.2] (standard evals are blind to it). Decision band: consistency in [0.4, 0.7) means drift is partly structured, partly noise -- reported as such; output-side correlation with |r| in (0.2, 0.4] means checks catch some drift, tempering the blind-spot claim. Negative: consistency < 0.4 (drift is essentially random across seeds) refutes H1's "lawful" premise -- a clean negative result warning against a-priori side-effect claims.

Experiment 2 (H2 -- A geometry-derived side-effect signature predicts the drift vector). Tests that an intervention-free signature computed from the SAE dictionary forecasts each feature's measured drift vector. Data/model: per feature compute (i) decoder-direction overlaps -- cosine of the feature's decoder direction with other property features' directions; (ii) a per-feature property-Jacobian -- gradient of each differentiable-surrogate property predictor w.r.t. residual-stream activations projected onto the feature direction. Predict the drift vector from these; correlate with the measured drift vector from Experiment 1; baselines -- concept-correlation and a chance permutation. Decisive metric (primary): cosine similarity / R^2 between predicted and actual drift vectors across features, plus per-property Spearman. Convincing positive: predicted-vs-actual drift cosine >= 0.6 (bootstrap CI excludes the concept-correlation baseline and chance) -- establishing lawfulness. Decision band: cosine in [0.35, 0.6) means the signature captures the dominant coupling but misses structure -- reported as partial law, usable for ranking not exact forecasting. Negative: cosine <= 0.35 (no better than concept-correlation/chance) means the drift is not predictable from dictionary geometry, refuting H2 (H1 may still hold descriptively).

Experiment 3 (H3 -- Pre-flight forecaster ranks features by collateral before generation). Tests that the signature ranks features by expected total collateral without any generation. Data/systems: use the signature to rank all target features by forecast total collateral for each target property; validate against the measured collateral from Experiment 1. Decisive metric: precision@k for selecting genuinely low-collateral features, and rank correlation (Spearman) between forecast and measured collateral. Convincing positive: precision@5 >= 0.8 and Spearman >= 0.6 (CI excludes 0), with quantified compute saved vs generation-based screening, plus a human-readable forecast per feature. Decision band: precision@5 in [0.6, 0.8) or Spearman in [0.4, 0.6) means the forecaster is a useful but imperfect screen -- reported with its error rate. Negative: precision@5 <= 0.6 means the ranking is not actionable, and the forecasting payoff is withdrawn.

Experiment 4 (H3 -- Minimal-collateral controller hits target while holding others fixed; positive control). Tests that selecting low-forecast-collateral features or orthogonalizing against held-fixed property axes Pareto-dominates naive steering. Data/systems: (a) select lowest-forecast-collateral feature for the target; (b) orthogonalize the steering direction against the property-Jacobian axes of properties to be held fixed; compare to naive best-concept-correlation steering on on-target gain, off-target drift on held-fixed properties, validity, novelty. POSITIVE CONTROL: two features constructed to share a decoder subspace (high overlap) and two known-orthogonal ones -- confirm the signature predicts high vs low cross-property drift. Decisive metric (primary): area of the target-gain-vs-collateral Pareto frontier, and held-fixed drift reduction at matched on-target gain. Convincing positive: orthogonalized/selected steering cuts held-fixed drift by >= 30% at matched on-target gain (Pareto-dominates naive), AND the positive control shows high-overlap pairs drift >= 3x more than orthogonal pairs. Decision band: held-fixed drift reduction in [10%, 30%), or on-target gain lost to achieve it, is a quantified trade rather than domination -- reported as such. Negative: no frontier improvement over naive steering (< 10% drift reduction), or a failed positive control, means the controller offers no practical collateral control and the applied claim fails.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) In-silico property oracles (ESMFold/DSSP, RDKit/SMARTS, biopython) are proxies for wet-lab truth; claims concern model-internal, structurally-defined off-target drift and its predictability, not experimental function. 2) The property-Jacobian requires a differentiable surrogate for properties measured by non-differentiable evaluators (HMMER motifs, folding); we quantify surrogate fidelity and also report the purely-geometric decoder-overlap predictor which needs no surrogate. 3) Off-target drift could be dominated by generic validity collapse rather than structured coupling; we isolate the regime where objects stay valid and report structured drift separately, using random-direction controls. 4) The law may be property-pair- or model-specific rather than universal; we test multiple properties, model sizes, and SAE variants and report where it fails—a negative/conditional result is still informative. 5) The orthogonalization fix may reduce on-target gain or interpretability; we quantify the tradeoff on the frontier rather than assume a free lunch. 6) SAE quality/layer choice could confound both drift and signature; controlled via multiple SAE variants, layers, difference-of-means baselines, and the positive control. 7) If drift turns out to be unpredictable noise, that is a clean, publishable negative result constraining theories of feature-dictionary geometry and warning against a-priori side-effect claims.

The mechanism claim (SAE geometry predicts off-target effects) is not itself new relative to close prior work; the delta is a harder domain plus full property-vector forecasting rather than fuzzy behavioral side effects.

Name: chirality_syntactic_shortcut
Title: A Tag, Not a Concept: Do String-Based Molecular Generators Represent Chirality Causally or Copy It as Syntax?
Short Hypothesis: String-based (SMILES/SELFIES) molecular generative models emit stereochemistry tokens (@/@@, E/Z) not because they possess a semantically-grounded internal representation of 3D chirality, but as a largely syntactic copy-from-context habit. We hypothesize that (i) there is NO compact, causally-steerable internal feature that flips a stereocenter's configuration while holding the rest of the molecule fixed; (ii) instead, the model tracks a shallow 'stereo-parity bookkeeping' signal tied to local ring/branch syntax; and (iii) this makes controlled enantiomer design (asking for the R vs S form of a specified scaffold) systematically unreliable in a way ordinary validity/property checks never reveal.
Related Work: Chirality is known to break geometric ML: 'E(3)-equivariant models cannot learn chirality' (2024) proves 3D-invariant GNNs discard it, and chirality-aware GNNs (MolKGNN 2023, ChiENN 2023, tetrahedral MPNNs 2020, ChiDeK 2026) add architecture to recover it. On the generative side, 'Stereochemistry-aware string-based molecular generation' (2025) shows string models CAN emit stereochemistry but says nothing about the internal mechanism. Mechanistic work on molecular transformers ('Circuits, Features, and Heuristics in Molecular Transformers' 2025) finds ring/branch syntax circuits and a steerable valence-capacity direction, and SynFlowNet interpretability (2025) finds decodable physicochemical features - but NEITHER examines chirality, the one property where 2D connectivity is uninformative and a genuine internal 3D concept would be required. No prior interpretability study asks whether a string-based generator's stereochemistry tokens are backed by a causal, steerable chirality representation or are a syntactic shortcut, nor audits controlled-enantiomer design reliability through this lens. This distinguishes the proposal from all prior chirality-architecture work (which changes the model) and from my own prior steering proposals (which assumed the target property has a genuine internal handle). Here the central claim is the ABSENCE of such a handle for the hardest, most safety-critical property.
Abstract: Chirality determines whether a drug heals or harms - enantiomers share identical 2D connectivity yet can differ drastically in safety and potency - and it is the one molecular property that cannot be read off a graph, requiring genuine 3D reasoning. String-based generative models (SMILES/SELFIES language models) routinely emit stereochemistry tokens (@/@@, E/Z) and pass validity checks, but it is unknown whether they possess an internal, causally-manipulable representation of chirality or merely copy stereo tags as local syntax. We surface and test this behavioral phenomenon. Training sparse autoencoders on autoregressive SMILES/SELFIES language models, we (1) LOCATE candidate chirality-encoding features/directions via probing for stereocenter configuration in the residual stream at the tokens surrounding a stereocenter; (2) CAUSALLY test whether any compact intervention flips a targeted stereocenter's configuration (R->S) in the finished molecule while holding the rest of the graph, other stereocenters, and validity fixed - the operational definition of a genuine chirality handle; (3) INTERPRET what the located units actually encode (true 3D parity vs shallow ring/branch syntactic bookkeeping) using controlled substrate pairs; and (4) AUDIT controlled-enantiomer design reliability - asking the model for a specified R or S form and measuring how often it silently returns the wrong enantiomer, the racemate, or migrates chirality to a different center, and whether validity/likelihood signals detect this. We predict no clean causal chirality handle exists, that stereo tokens ride local syntax, and that enantiocontrol fails silently - recasting a routinely-reported model capability as a safety-critical blind spot, and yielding a diagnostic for when generated stereochemistry can be trusted.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: autoregressive SMILES and SELFIES language models (~90M parameters), trained by us (or public checkpoints where available) on a stereochemistry-rich subset of ChEMBL/PubChem that retains @/@@ and E/Z tags (~2M molecules with defined stereocenters); two model sizes (~30M, ~90M) for scaling. Base weights frozen. SAEs: TopK (k=32, dictionary 16384) on mid-layer residual streams (two layers), seeds {0,1}, FVU reported. Ground truth via RDKit: canonical CIP labels (R/S) per stereocenter, E/Z per double bond, enantiomer/diastereomer relations. Validity gates: RDKit-parseable, valence-valid, stereochemically well-defined (no undefined-but-implied centers). Interventions: SAE-feature clamp/steer, difference-of-means (R-minus-S) direction, and enantiomer activation-patching; norm-matched random-direction and matched-non-chirality-feature controls; strength swept.

Experiment 0/1 (H1 -- Baseline that stereochemistry is genuinely emitted, then: is chirality decodable?). Establishes that the model emits correct, non-trivial stereochemistry (so a later null steering result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact), and locates candidate chirality directions. Data: 5,000 generated valid molecules with defined stereocenters; 2,000 held-out natural molecules for probing. Baseline metric: fraction of generated stereocenters whose CIP label matches a chemically sensible completion and stereo-token accuracy vs a copy-context null. Probing: at token positions surrounding each stereocenter, train linear/MLP probes to predict CIP R/S from residual activations and from SAE features; report AUROC vs generation-progress and layer, against an SAE-independent raw-activation probe AND against a purely syntactic control probe (predict whether the next stereo token is @ vs @@ from the partial string). Decisive metric: chirality-probe AUROC minus syntax-probe AUROC. Convincing baseline+location: model stereo-token accuracy clearly above the copy-context null AND chirality-probe AUROC>=0.75. Decision band: chirality-minus-syntax AUROC gap in [0.0, 0.1] means the "chirality" decodability is largely syntax prediction -- flagged, and location is treated as syntactic. Negative baseline: if the model does not emit correct stereochemistry above the copy null, the study is under-powered for absence claims and reported as inconclusive rather than confirming H1.

Experiment 2 (H1 -- No compact causal stereocenter-flip handle). Tests whether any compact intervention flips a targeted stereocenter R->S while holding the rest of the graph, other centers, and validity fixed. Data: 3,000 single-stereocenter molecules and 1,500 multi-stereocenter molecules. Systems: SAE-feature intervention, difference-of-means direction, and enantiomer activation-patching, each vs random-direction and matched-non-chirality-feature controls; dose-response swept. Decisive metric (primary): ENANTIOFLIP SUCCESS RATE = fraction of interventions producing the exact mirror configuration at the TARGET center while (a) keeping the 2D graph identical, (b) leaving other centers unchanged, (c) preserving validity. Convincing support for H1 (no handle): best-intervention enantioflip success <= 15% (barely above the random-direction control) despite the confirmed baseline, with failures dominated by graph corruption / wrong-center flips / racemization. Decision band: success in (15%, 40%] is a PARTIAL/UNRELIABLE handle -- reported as neither clean absence nor clean presence; center-specificity (multi-center bleed rate) decides how it is framed. Negative (refutes H1): success >= 40% with high specificity means a genuine steerable chirality handle EXISTS -- an equally publishable positive finding that overturns the hypothesis.

Experiment 3 (H2 -- The signal is shallow syntactic parity bookkeeping, not 3D parity). Tests whether the located units track true CIP parity or local @/@@ ring/branch syntax. Data: controlled substrate pairs -- (i) molecules where the same @/@@ token maps to opposite CIP labels depending on neighbor ordering, and (ii) matched pairs where CIP label is constant but ring/branch context varies; plus SMILES-rewriting/canonicalization that preserves the molecule. Decisive metric: feature-meaning INVARIANCE under molecule-preserving SMILES rewriting = correlation of feature activation with true CIP parity vs with raw @/@@ syntax. Convincing support for H2: feature tracks raw syntax (syntax correlation >= 0.7) and flips meaning under rewriting (CIP-parity correlation <= 0.3). Decision band: mixed loadings (both correlations in [0.3, 0.7)) means the unit is partly conceptual, partly syntactic -- reported as intermediate, not a clean shortcut. Negative: feature stays invariant to rewriting and tracks true CIP parity (parity correlation >= 0.7) means the model has a genuine 3D-parity representation, refuting H2.

Experiment 4 (H3 -- Controlled-enantiomer design is silently unreliable, missed by output-side checks). Tests that requesting a specified enantiomer often returns the wrong one and that validity/likelihood do not detect it while an internal probe does. Data: request a SPECIFIED enantiomer of given scaffolds, stratified by number of stereocenters and scaffold complexity; 3,000 requests. Decisive metric (primary): SILENT ENANTIO-ERROR RATE = fraction of valid outputs returning the wrong enantiomer, opposite/undefined configuration, racemate, or chirality at a different center; secondary: detection AUROC/calibration of output-side signals (RDKit-validity, likelihood/perplexity, a property-predictor's confidence) vs the internal chirality-probe score from Experiment 1 for catching wrong-enantiomer outputs. Convincing positive: silent enantio-error rate rising with stereocenter count to >= 30% at >=2 centers, with output-side detection AUROC in [0.45, 0.60] (near chance) while the internal probe reaches AUROC>=0.75 -- a usable pre-flight enantioreliability filter. Decision band: error rate in [15%, 30%) means unreliability is present but modest; internal-probe AUROC in [0.6, 0.75) is a weak filter -- reported with its error. Negative: error rate < 15% and output-side signals already detect errors (AUROC>=0.7) means enantiocontrol is reliable / already checkable, refuting H3. Robustness across SMILES vs SELFIES, two model sizes, two SAE variants, and E/Z stereochemistry; test whether enantioflip success or error rate improves with scale or training stereochemistry density.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The core claim is partly an ABSENCE claim (no clean causal handle), which requires strong effort to steer before concluding failure; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (SAE features, difference-of-means, enantiomer activation-patching), sweeping strength, and requiring the baseline in step 1 to confirm the model does emit correct stereochemistry - so a null enantioflip is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. 2) A positive result (a genuine steerable chirality handle exists) is equally publishable and would itself be a novel, useful finding for stereocontrolled design. 3) Stereochemistry ground truth relies on RDKit CIP assignment, which can be ambiguous for exotic centers; we restrict to well-defined central and E/Z stereochemistry and report assignment confidence. 4) Claims concern model-internal representation and string-level stereochemistry, not wet-lab bioactivity; the safety framing is about reliably producing the REQUESTED enantiomer, an objective structural fact. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound location; controlled with multiple SAE variants, layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 6) SMILES/SELFIES tokenization differences may complicate cross-encoding comparison; we standardize the stereochemistry evaluation on RDKit-parsed finished molecules. 7) An internal probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; even so, the interpretability (syntactic-vs-conceptual diagnosis) and the reliability-audit payoff are the contributions and are reported honestly.

novelty.reasoning: The core idea is not a new chirality mechanism per se; it is a mechanistic/causal audit of whether string models learn chirality or just syntax. That delta is narrower because recent work already gives a mechanistic account of chirality emergence and chiral-sensitive head ablations. The potentially novel pieces are the SAE-based causal enantioflip test, the SMILES-rewriting invariance analysis, and the design-reliability framing. So novelty is real but mostly in the diagnostic/controllability claim, not the underlying phenomenon.

Name: symmetry_shortcut_crystal
Title: Symmetry Without Understanding? Auditing Whether Crystal Generative Models Causally Represent Space-Group Constraints or Silently Fake Them
Short Hypothesis: Crystal generative models conditioned on a target space group satisfy the constraint not because they possess a compact, causally-manipulable internal representation of the requested symmetry, but via a shallow lattice/Wyckoff-copying shortcut. We hypothesize (i) there is a decodable but only weakly causally-steerable internal 'space-group' direction; (ii) steering it to request a NEW space group frequently yields structures whose achieved symmetry silently mismatches the request (wrong space group, lower symmetry, or broken periodicity) while still passing validity/stability checks; and (iii) an intervention-free internal symmetry-consistency signal predicts these silent failures better than output-side likelihood or formation-energy proxies.
Related Work: Symmetry-aware crystal generation is a rich area: SymmCD (2025), DiffCSP++/Space-Group-Constrained Generation (2024), WyCryst (2023), and PGCGM (2022) either hard-code space-group/Wyckoff constraints or condition on them. Critically, Ishii et al. (2026, WyckoffDiff-Adaptor) show that conditional symmetry control 'may not be sufficiently effective when space group constraints are applied as a condition'—i.e., models silently violate the requested symmetry—but treat this as an architecture problem, not a representational one. Interpretability in materials (CGCNN 2018, Site-Net 2022, RankAAE 2023) is confined to PREDICTIVE property models with attention/latent-descriptor analysis; none examines the internal mechanism of GENERATIVE crystal models, and none asks whether symmetry—the defining, physics-critical property of crystals—is a genuine causal handle or a copying shortcut. No prior work (a) locates and causally tests a space-group representation inside a crystal generator, (b) shows symmetry-conditioned generation silently fakes the requested symmetry via a shortcut, or (c) provides an internal symmetry-reliability audit that catches these failures. This distinguishes the proposal from all symmetry-architecture work (which changes the model) and mirrors, in a new object class and for a new property (crystallographic symmetry vs stereochemistry), the shortcut-auditing lens of prior molecular proposals.
Abstract: Symmetry is the defining property of a crystal: its space group dictates physical behavior and is the primary control knob in modern crystal generative models, which either hard-code it or condition on it. Yet recent evidence shows conditional symmetry control can silently fail—models emit structures that do not have the requested space group. We ask a mechanistic question no prior work addresses: do crystal generators actually possess an internal, causally-manipulable representation of the requested symmetry, or do they satisfy the constraint through a shallow lattice/Wyckoff-copying shortcut that mimics symmetry without understanding it? Using open symmetry-conditioned diffusion generators (e.g., DiffCSP++/SymmCD-style models) trained on Materials Project data, we (1) LOCATE candidate space-group representations by probing the denoiser's internal activations for the target space group and lattice class; (2) CAUSALLY test whether a compact intervention can convert generation from one space group to another—producing a structure whose ACHIEVED symmetry (verified by pymatgen SpacegroupAnalyzer at tolerance sweeps) matches the new request while composition and validity are preserved—the operational definition of a genuine symmetry handle; (3) INTERPRET whether the located units encode true symmetry (invariant to equivalent lattice re-descriptions and origin choices) or shallow lattice-parameter/Wyckoff-token statistics; and (4) AUDIT symmetry-conditioned design reliability, measuring the SILENT SYMMETRY-ERROR RATE—requested-vs-achieved space-group mismatches that pass validity/stability screens—and whether an intervention-free internal symmetry-consistency score flags them better than likelihood or formation-energy proxies. Results would recast a headline capability of crystal generators as a potentially unreliable shortcut and deliver a cheap pre-flight symmetry-trust filter for materials design.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models: open symmetry-conditioned crystal diffusion generators with accessible per-step denoiser activations -- a coordinate-based diffusion (DiffCSP++-style) and a Wyckoff-based diffusion (SymmCD/WyckoffDiff-style) checkpoint, trained on Materials Project / MP-20. Base weights frozen; only probes/SAEs trained. Achieved-symmetry ground truth: pymatgen SpacegroupAnalyzer over a tolerance sweep (record achieved space group, crystal system, point group, Wyckoff multiplicities). Validity gates: bond-length/overlap checks, charge neutrality, StructureMatcher novelty; stability proxy = energy-above-hull from a pretrained universal ML interatomic potential (CHGNet/MACE-MP), NO DFT. Probes: linear/MLP on denoiser residual activations at multiple timesteps/layers; difference-of-means directions and full activation-patching for intervention; norm-matched random-direction and matched-non-symmetry-feature controls. 500 generations per condition.

Experiment 0/1 (H1 -- Baseline reproduction, then: is the space group decodable?). Establishes that the model unconditionally reproduces target space groups above chance (so absence/weak-steerability claims are meaningful) and that space group is decodable internally. Data: 5,000 conditioned generations spanning the space-group vocabulary; probes trained on denoiser activations. Baseline metric: requested-vs-achieved space-group match rate vs a frequency-matched random-request chance level. Decoding: probe accuracy for target space group, crystal system, and lattice class vs timestep/layer, against a control probe that predicts the raw conditioning-token embedding (to gauge trivial copy-of-condition). Decisive metric: symmetry-probe accuracy minus condition-copy-probe accuracy. Convincing baseline+decodability: baseline match rate clearly above chance AND space-group probe accuracy >= 0.7 that exceeds the condition-copy control by >= 0.1. Decision band: probe-minus-copy gap in [0.0, 0.1] means the decodable signal is largely a copy of the conditioning input -- flagged. Negative baseline: if the model does not reproduce target space groups above chance, the study is under-powered for the steerability claim and reported as inconclusive.

Experiment 2 (H1 -- The space-group direction is only WEAKLY causally steerable). Tests whether intervening on the decoded direction switches the achieved space group from A to B. Data/systems: generations conditioned on space group A; intervene via probe-derived direction, difference-of-means (B-minus-A), and full activation-patching from a B-conditioned run, vs random-direction and matched-non-symmetry controls; dose-response swept. Decisive metric (primary): SYMMETRY-SWITCH SUCCESS RATE = fraction of interventions yielding a finished structure whose SpacegroupAnalyzer symmetry equals B while composition and validity/stability are preserved and the change is specific. Convincing support for H1 (decodable-but-weakly-steerable): switch success in (5%, 40%] -- clearly above the random control (weakly causal) yet far below the conditioning baseline's match rate -- with failures skewed to subgroups of A/B. Decision band: success <= 5% means essentially NO causal handle (stronger than "weak"); >= 40% with specificity means a GENUINE strong handle -- either extreme is reported as such rather than as the hypothesized weak-steerability. Negative for the phenomenon: a strong, specific handle (>=40%) refutes the shortcut framing and is an equally publishable positive finding.

Experiment 3 (H2 -- Silent symmetry mismatches that pass validity/stability). Tests that requesting a new space group frequently yields valid+stable structures whose achieved symmetry silently differs from the request. Data/systems: across the full space-group vocabulary (stratified by crystal system, symmetry order, and training frequency), request each space group; among VALID+stable outputs measure the mismatch. Decisive metric (primary): SILENT SYMMETRY-ERROR RATE = fraction of valid+stable outputs whose achieved space group differs from requested, decomposed into correct-crystal-system-but-wrong-group, dropped-to-subgroup, and fully-broken-symmetry, stratified by requested symmetry order and training frequency. Convincing positive: silent error rate rising with symmetry order to >= 30% for high-symmetry / low-frequency requests, tolerance-robust across the SpacegroupAnalyzer sweep. Decision band: error rate in [15%, 30%) means mismatch exists but is modest -- reported as such; error rate that flips sign of conclusion across tolerances is reported as tolerance-sensitive and excluded from strong claims. Negative: error rate < 15% (models reliably achieve the requested symmetry) refutes H2. Interpretation sub-test (supports H1/H2): controlled crystal pairs dissociating space group from surface descriptors (same group / different lattice params or origin; different groups / similar lattice params) test whether the located feature is invariant to equivalent cell re-descriptions (true symmetry) or tracks lattice-parameter/Wyckoff-token statistics (shortcut) -- a feature that changes meaning under symmetry-preserving re-description is scored as a shortcut.

Experiment 4 (H3 -- Internal symmetry-consistency signal beats output-side proxies at flagging silent failures). Tests that an intervention-free internal signal predicts silent symmetry errors better than likelihood or formation-energy proxies. Data/systems: for each generation compute an internal symmetry-consistency score (probe confidence / feature coherence read mid-generation); baselines -- generation likelihood, e-above-hull/formation-energy proxy, validity checks, and a black-box raw-activation probe; target label = silent symmetry error from Experiment 3. Decisive metric (primary): detection AUROC and calibration ECE for flagging silent symmetry errors. Convincing positive: internal-signal AUROC >= 0.80 with ECE<=0.10 while output-side likelihood/energy proxies stay in [0.45, 0.60] (near chance), with quantified compute saved by aborting untrustworthy requests before full generation + relaxation. Decision band: internal AUROC in [0.65, 0.80), or its edge over the black-box probe in [0.03, 0.10) AUROC, means the internal signal works but its advantage over cheaper signals is marginal -- the interpretability (shortcut-vs-concept) diagnosis is then the contribution. Negative: output-side proxies already reach AUROC>=0.70, or the internal signal fails to beat them, refutes H3. Robustness across the two generator architectures, two tolerances, and high- vs low-symmetry groups.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The core claim is partly an ABSENCE claim (no clean causal symmetry handle); we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (probe direction, difference-of-means, full activation patching), sweeping strength, and requiring the step-1 baseline to confirm the model does reproduce target space groups—so a null switch result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable symmetry handle) is equally publishable and useful for symmetry-controlled design. 2) Achieved-symmetry ground truth depends on SpacegroupAnalyzer tolerance; we sweep tolerances and report sensitivity, restricting strong claims to tolerance-robust cases. 3) Stability is assessed by ML interatomic potentials (CHGNet/MACE), an in-silico proxy for DFT/synthesizability; claims concern requested-vs-achieved symmetry (an objective crystallographic fact) and model-internal representation, not experimental synthesizability. 4) Requires generators with accessible per-step activations; scope limited to open, instrumentable models. 5) An internal probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; even so, the interpretability diagnosis (shortcut vs concept) and the reliability-audit payoff are the contributions and are reported honestly. 6) Symmetry and lattice statistics may be irreducibly entangled for some space groups; the controlled re-description pairs (step 4) are designed to separate them and we report where separation is impossible.

novelty.reasoning: Core claims needing novelty are: (1) symmetry-conditioned crystal generators may rely on shallow lattice/Wyckoff shortcuts rather than a causally usable internal space-group concept; (2) one can locate and causally test an internal space-group representation in generative crystal models via probing/intervention on denoiser activations; (3) silent requested-vs-achieved symmetry mismatch persists even when outputs pass validity/stability filters; (4) an intervention-free internal symmetry-consistency signal can predict such failures better than output-side proxies; and (5) invariance tests can distinguish true symmetry representation from superficial statistics. From the proposal plus search summary, the failure phenomenon itself is not new: prior crystal generation work already documents poor space-group adherence. The novelty instead lies in the mechanistic/representational explanation, causal testing inside generative crystal models, and the auditing formulation. That is a meaningful delta from prior architecture-focused work and from interpretability work limited to predictive materials models. Relative to the cited related work, this is more than an obvious benchmark extension, though it borrows established mechanistic-interpretability tools and applies them to a new domain. Closest prior family is symmetry-conditioned crystal generators showing weak symmetry control, plus materials-model interpretability; actual delta is causal localization/testing of internal symmetry representations and an internal reliability audit for generative symmetry compliance.

impact.reasoning: The problem under study is reliability of symmetry-conditioned crystal generation: whether requested crystallographic symmetry is truly achieved and whether internal signals can flag silent failures before downstream use. The community that would care is the crystal/materials generative-design community, especially researchers using space group as a control knob for materials discovery. If the result holds, it could change how papers evaluate conditional crystal generation, pushing the field to report requested-vs-achieved symmetry, internal reliability diagnostics, and perhaps distrust naive symmetry conditioning. Strongest one-line case: a model can appear chemically valid yet silently violate the very symmetry constraint users believe they controlled. This is a real and timely problem, not a mere curiosity, but it is still somewhat concentrated within a specialized subfield. Follow-up work would likely cite it for evaluation methodology and mechanistic diagnosis. It could moderately shift direction by reframing a capability claim from architecture success to representation reliability. Real-world reach is indirect but relevant for materials design workflows. Passing the 'so what?' test: yes, if silent mismatch is common and detectable internally, serious researchers would change evaluation protocols and practitioners would add symmetry audits before trusting generated candidates.

review.reasoning: This is a thoughtful, fairly testable proposal with unusually concrete experiments, thresholds, controls, and negative-result handling. The hypotheses are falsifiable and scoped better than most early-stage proposals. Major strengths are the explicit decision bands, multiple intervention types, robustness to tolerance sweeps, and architecture diversity. Main weaknesses: several thresholds (e.g., probe >=0.7, switch success 5-40%, AUROC >=0.80) appear somewhat arbitrary and not justified by prior calibration; the operationalization of 'genuine symmetry handle' may still confound condition copying, composition changes, or trajectory-level effects; activation interventions in diffusion models are technically delicate and may fail for reasons unrelated to absent representation; the proposal depends heavily on SpacegroupAnalyzer settings and proxy stability models; and the related work, while decent, should more specifically position against any existing representation/probing work in generative diffusion models outside materials. Some controls are still missing: stronger causal controls for preserving non-symmetry attributes, tests against simpler output-side symmetry heuristics, and analysis of whether probe success merely tracks timestep or denoising progress. If executed well, this could be strong enough for a serious ML venue as a mechanistic analysis paper, though likely more as a specialized ML-for-science or interpretability contribution than a top-tier broad method breakthrough. Minimum viable edits are mostly about tightening causal claims, justifying thresholds, and specifying missing controls.
