Name: epistasis_steering_blindspot
Title: Levers for Positions, Not for Couplings: Can Interpretable Features Causally Control Epistasis in Protein Language Models?
Short Hypothesis: Interpretable sparse-autoencoder features of protein language models give causal, steerable control over SINGLE-POSITION (additive) sequence properties, but NOT over EPISTASIS — the context-dependent coupling that makes one position's optimal residue depend on another. We hypothesize that steering a feature to install a desired coupling (e.g., a compensatory residue pair, an allosteric linkage) silently produces sequences whose additive properties change while the intended coupling structure fails to form, an 'epistasis blind spot' that single-mutant checks miss but a double-mutant-cycle oracle exposes.
Related Work: pLM interpretability/steering work (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; Steering PLMs/ASPO 2025; antibody-SAE 2025; ProtoMech 2026; Automated Neuron Labelling 2025; SAEs for low-N design 2025) discovers and steers features that all encode INTRINSIC, single-position or local-motif properties (secondary structure, GRAVY, molecular weight, zinc-finger motifs, thermostability) and evaluate whether that standalone property appears. Separately, a distinct biology literature establishes that pLMs INTERNALLY capture epistasis: ESM-2 stores coevolving-residue statistics like a Markov Random Field (Zhang et al. 2024), pLMs capture both structural-contact and long-range FUNCTIONAL couplings zero-shot (2025), and higher-order epistasis is present in sequence-function models (2024). Crucially, no work connects these: none asks whether the epistatic/coupling structure pLMs demonstrably represent is a CAUSALLY STEERABLE design lever, contrasts coupling-steerability against single-position steerability, or audits when a designer's coupling request silently fails. This distinguishes the proposal from all single-property steering work (which assumes an additive target) and from the epistasis-probing literature (which is purely descriptive/predictive, never touching feature-level steering of generation). Epistasis is the ideal testbed because it has an exact, well-established quantitative oracle — the double-mutant cycle (epistasis = ddG_AB - ddG_A - ddG_B) computable from deep mutational scanning (DMS) data or in-silico stability predictors.
Abstract: A protein's function is shaped not only by which residue sits at each position but by epistasis: the coupling that makes the best residue at one position depend on another, underlying compensatory mutations, allosteric linkages, and folding cooperativity. Interpretability-guided protein design increasingly steers language-model features to install desired properties, and pLMs are known to internally capture epistatic couplings — yet every demonstrated steering target is an additive, single-position property. We ask whether interpretable features can causally control epistasis at all, or only additive traits. We surface a behavioral phenomenon we call the epistasis blind spot: steering a feature to install a target coupling (a compensatory residue pair, a contact-based or long-range functional linkage) reliably shifts additive properties while the intended coupling structure fails to form — invisible to single-mutant and validity checks but exposed by a double-mutant-cycle oracle. Epistasis is uniquely suited to this question because it is exactly quantifiable (epistasis = ddG_AB - ddG_A - ddG_B) from deep mutational scanning data and in-silico stability predictors. Using ESM-2 with TopK and Ordered sparse autoencoders, we (1) LOCATE candidate additive-property features and candidate coupling/epistasis features via probing (single-position vs pairwise-coupling signals); (2) CAUSALLY test the steerability of each, contrasting additive control against coupling control; (3) quantify the blind spot; and (4) AUDIT reliability, testing whether an internal coupling-consistency signal flags silently-uncoupled designs better than single-mutant or likelihood checks. We predict additive control succeeds, coupling control is decodable-but-weakly-steerable, and a cheap internal audit catches epistasis blind spots before expensive validation.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (FROZEN): ESM-2 (150M and 650M); generation by masked infilling. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered SAEs (Ordered can recover steerability TopK lacks), expansion 16x, k=32, 30M residual-stream activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, seeds 0/1/2. ADDITIVE oracles: single-mutant effect on GRAVY, net charge, and a stability proxy (fine-tuned ddG head or FoldX), plus ESM-2 single-mutant log-likelihood. EPISTASIS oracle (exact operational definition): the double-mutant-cycle term epsilon = ddG_AB - ddG_A - ddG_B, taken from combinatorial deep-mutational-scanning (DMS) landscapes with measured double mutants - GB1 (Olson 2014, ~535,000 double mutants) plus 2-3 further combinatorial-DMS landscapes from ProteinGym-style resources - and from FoldX for position pairs not experimentally covered; the pLM categorical-Jacobian gives an internal pairwise-coupling read. In-silico epsilon is validated against measured doubles on the DMS-covered subset and strong claims restricted to where they agree. Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity. First confirm the model natively spans a meaningful RANGE of couplings. Steering = add alpha*d_hat during infilling; alpha over {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - single-position (additive) features are causally steerable): Identify additive features (correlate with a single position's property, controlling for context; probe AUROC/R^2) and steer to raise a target additive property (e.g., GRAVY) at a chosen position. Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: on-target additive effect size (Cohen's d, steered vs unsteered, within the validity budget). Decision band: d >= 0.8 AND >= 0.4 over control for >=2/3 of features => additive control genuine (H1 holds); [0.2,0.4) over control => inconclusive; < 0.2 => not steerable (premise fails).

Experiment 2 (H2 - epistasis is decodable-but-not-steerable, and steering to install a coupling silently changes additive properties while the coupling fails to form): (a) DECODABILITY: probe the pairwise epistasis magnitude / categorical-Jacobian coupling of a position pair, controlling for the two positions' additive effects via partial correlation; AUROC. (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head: steer the best coupling direction (TopK/Ordered SAE feature, difference-of-means high-vs-low-coupling, activation-patching from strongly-coupled sequences, additive-orthogonalized direction) to install a target epistasis at a position pair while holding the two positions' additive contributions fixed. Decisive metrics FIRST: SILENT-DECOUPLING RATE = fraction of coupling-steered, valid sequences whose double-mutant-cycle epsilon did not form (|Delta epsilon| below oracle noise) or formed wrong-sign while additive properties shifted; and ratio r = coupling efficacy / additive efficacy from Experiment 1. Decision band: coupling decodable (AUROC >= 0.70) AND r <= 0.33 AND decoupling >= 0.30 => epistasis blind spot confirmed; r in (0.33,0.67) => partial (test Ordered SAEs); r >= 0.67 => a steerable epistasis handle exists, refuting H2 (equally publishable).

Experiment 3 (H3 - single-mutant checks miss the failure but the exact double-mutant-cycle oracle exposes it): For the Experiment-2 sequences, compare what a practitioner would inspect against ground truth. Decisive metric FIRST: Spearman rho between the additive-property change / single-mutant scores / pseudo-perplexity and the true change in double-mutant-cycle epsilon. Decision band: |rho| <= 0.20 => single-mutant checks are blind to the coupling failure while the double-mutant-cycle oracle reveals it (H3 confirmed); |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial visibility; |rho| >= 0.40 => single-mutant checks already flag it (weakens the blind-spot framing). ROBUSTNESS: two model sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, contact-based (short-range) vs long-range functional couplings; test whether steerability is worse long-range than for contacts; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Epistasis has an exact operational definition (double-mutant cycle), but its measurement relies on either DMS data (limited combinatorial double-mutant coverage) or in-silico stability predictors (FoldX/Rosetta), which are proxies; we validate in-silico epistasis against measured double mutants on the DMS-covered subset and restrict strong claims to where they agree, framing claims as model-internal, oracle-verified coupling controllability rather than wet-lab function. 2) The coupling-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (TopK and Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching, additive-orthogonalized directions), sweeping strength, requiring the model to natively span an epistasis range, and head-to-head calibrating that ADDITIVE features ARE steerable in the same pipeline — so a null coupling result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable epistasis handle) is equally publishable and directly enables compensatory/allosteric design. 3) Additive and epistatic effects are partly entangled; the partial-correlation feature selection and additive-matched dissociation pairs (step 5) isolate genuinely additive-independent coupling signal, and we report where separation is impossible. 4) Double-mutant-cycle evaluation is combinatorially heavier than single-mutant checks; we cap position pairs and use the internal audit precisely to reduce this cost. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes (categorical Jacobian), and random-direction controls. 6) An internal coupling probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (additive-steerable, epistasis-decodable-but-weakly-steerable) and the audit payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 7) If coupling steering unexpectedly succeeds, it overturns the hypothesis but yields a strong positive finding that pLM epistasis is a controllable design lever.

Name: magnitude_dial_blindspot
Title: On/Off but Not How-Much: Do Interpretable Features Give a Calibrated Magnitude Dial for Scientific Design, or Only a Presence Switch?
Short Hypothesis: Scientific sequence/graph generative models represent a design property's categorical PRESENCE as a cleanly causally-steerable feature, but do NOT possess a calibrated internal representation of its quantitative MAGNITUDE: steering moves the property monotonically yet cannot dial it to a specified numeric target, and the internal magnitude code is logarithmically compressed so control degrades sharply at high magnitudes. Consequently 'set logP to 2.5' or 'set helix content to 40%' silently misses the target while presence/validity checks pass.
Related Work: A robust cognitive-science-inspired line shows LLMs encode numeric magnitude in low-dimensional, logarithmically-compressed, causally-manipulable subspaces (Language Models Represent Space and Time 2023; The Geometry of Numerical Reasoning 2024, which causally intervenes on numeric-comparison subspaces; Number Representations in LLMs 2025 showing sublinear/log compression; Numeric Magnitude Comparison Effects 2023 showing human-like distance/size effects). Separately, interpretability-of-generation for scientific objects (InterPLM 2024; ProtSAE 2025; chemistry-LM SAEs 2025; Steering PLMs/ASPO 2025) steers features toward a property and evaluates whether the property is INCREASED or PRESENT, always reporting directional/binary gains and never a QUANTITATIVE set-point. No prior work (a) transfers the log-compressed magnitude-representation phenomenon from text LLMs into scientific GENERATIVE design, (b) distinguishes presence-steerability from calibrated magnitude-steerability for the same property, or (c) exposes that hitting a numeric design set-point is an unrecognized blind spot with a level-dependent (worse-at-high-magnitude) failure profile. This is distinct from my prior proposals, which contrast intrinsic vs relational/global/pathway properties; here the contrast is categorical presence vs quantitative magnitude of the SAME property, and it borrows a specific human-numeracy finding.
Abstract: Real scientific design specifies numbers, not directions: a chemist needs logP = 2.5, an enzyme engineer needs 40% helix content, not merely 'more'. Interpretability-guided design increasingly steers language-model features to hit properties, but every demonstrated result reports only that the property increased or appeared. We ask whether interpretable features actually provide a CALIBRATED MAGNITUDE DIAL or merely a PRESENCE SWITCH. Borrowing a well-established cognitive-science result—that language models encode numeric magnitude in a logarithmically-compressed, causally-manipulable subspace—we test whether scientific generative models inherit this and whether it undermines quantitative controllability. We surface a behavioral phenomenon we call the magnitude blind spot: steering an interpretable feature moves a property monotonically but cannot reliably reach a specified numeric set-point, and control error grows systematically at high magnitudes, mirroring log compression. Using ESM-2 protein language models and a SMILES chemical language model with sparse autoencoders and exact quantitative oracles (RDKit logP/MW/TPSA; DSSP helix/sheet fraction; GRAVY), we (1) LOCATE candidate presence features and candidate magnitude directions via probing (classification vs regression, and testing for log-scaled geometry); (2) CAUSALLY test presence-steerability vs calibrated magnitude-steerability by asking each feature to hit graded numeric targets and measuring set-point error; (3) INTERPRET whether the magnitude code is linear or log-compressed and whether re-parameterizing steering by log-magnitude restores calibration; and (4) AUDIT reliability, testing whether an internal magnitude-consistency signal flags off-target designs better than presence/validity checks. We predict presence control succeeds, calibrated magnitude control fails—worse at high values—and a simple log-reparameterized dial recovers much of the lost precision.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (FROZEN): ESM-2 (150M/650M) for proteins and a GPT-style SMILES chemical LM (~15M params) for molecules. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered SAEs (Ordered can recover steerability TopK's decodable-but-inert features lack), expansion 16x, k=32, 30M activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, seeds 0/1/2. Properties are chosen to have EXACT continuous oracles so 'magnitude' is unambiguous: molecules - logP, molecular weight, TPSA, aromatic-ring count (RDKit); proteins - alpha-helix and beta-sheet fraction (DSSP on ESMFold), GRAVY. Validity gates: RDKit-validity + synthetic accessibility (molecules), ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity (proteins). Data: 20,000 held-out objects per domain to fit probes/directions; first confirm the frozen model natively spans a wide magnitude RANGE per property. Steering = add alpha*d_hat; alpha searched over a dense grid within the validity budget per target.

Experiment 1 (H1 - categorical PRESENCE is cleanly, causally steerable): On held-out objects, train a presence classifier (property above/below median) from SAE features and raw activations and identify the top presence feature. Steer to push the property across the median (the presence task). Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: presence-flip success rate. Decision band: success >= 0.80 AND >= 0.40 over random control for >=2/3 of properties => presence is a clean handle (H1 holds); [0.15,0.40) over control => inconclusive; < 0.15 => presence not steerable (premise fails).

Experiment 2 (H2 - the internal magnitude code is not calibrated: steering is monotone yet cannot dial to a specified numeric target): For each property, define a ladder of numeric set-points spanning the native range (e.g., logP = -1, 1, 3, 5). Steer the top magnitude direction (difference-of-means high-vs-low bins and regression-weight direction) and search alpha to best hit each target. Decisive metric FIRST: SET-POINT HIT-RATE within a tolerance band (logP +/-0.5; helix-fraction +/-0.05), plus the mean |achieved - requested| SET-POINT ERROR and a monotonicity check Spearman(alpha, property). Decision band: property is monotone in alpha (rho >= 0.90) BUT hit-rate <= 0.40 AND the presence-vs-set-point success gap >= 0.40 => monotone-but-uncalibrated confirmed (H2); hit-rate in (0.40,0.60) => partial; hit-rate >= 0.60 => a calibrated dial exists out of the box, refuting H2.

Experiment 3 (H3 - the magnitude code is logarithmically compressed, so control degrades sharply at high magnitudes): Fit both linear and log(value) regressions of the property on steering displacement and compare fits; regress SET-POINT ERROR on the requested magnitude. Decisive metric FIRST: the slope of set-point error vs requested magnitude, and the log-vs-linear Delta-R^2. Decision band: error slope > 0 with 95% CI excluding 0 (error grows with magnitude) AND log-fit Delta-R^2 >= 0.10 over linear => log-compression confirmed (H3); slope CI crossing 0 or Delta-R^2 in (0.03,0.10) => inconclusive; flat error and Delta-R^2 <= 0.03 => not log-compressed (refutes H3).

Experiment 4 (H4 - the miss is a blind spot: presence/validity checks pass while the number is wrong): Decisive metric FIRST: Spearman rho between output-side checks (validity, presence-classifier confidence, pseudo-perplexity, model likelihood) and the true set-point error from Experiment 2. Decision band: |rho| <= 0.20 => checks pass while the number is wrong (blind spot confirmed); |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; |rho| >= 0.40 => checks already reveal the miss (weakens H4). ROBUSTNESS: both domains, two model sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, multiple properties; report where the compression exponent and blind spot are stable vs artifact; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Property oracles differ in exactness—RDKit logP/MW/TPSA are effectively exact for the definition, while DSSP-on-ESMFold helix fraction is a structure-prediction proxy; we lead with the exact molecular oracles for core claims and treat protein results as corroborating, reporting oracle fidelity. 2) The magnitude-blind-spot is partly an ABSENCE-of-calibration claim; we mitigate by trying multiple directions (SAE feature, difference-of-means, regression-weight), TopK and Ordered SAEs, strength search per target, and by head-to-head confirming the PRESENCE task succeeds in the same pipeline—so failure to hit numbers is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuinely calibrated dial exists) is equally publishable. 3) Set-point error could be confounded by validity collapse near range extremes; we restrict to strengths within the validity budget and separately report the in-validity error curve. 4) The log-reparameterization fix could merely fit noise; we fit the calibration on a held-out strength sweep and evaluate on unseen targets, and report the exponent's stability across seeds. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with multiple SAE variants, layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 6) An internal magnitude probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (presence-steerable, magnitude-log-compressed-and-uncalibrated) and the calibration fix and audit payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 7) If calibrated set-point control already works out of the box, that is a valuable positive result establishing that interpretable features provide a usable quantitative dial for scientific design.

novelty.reasoning: Core claims are: (1) scientific generative models may support clean presence steering but not calibrated numeric set-point control; (2) the same property may be encoded in a log-compressed magnitude subspace; (3) steering error worsens at high target magnitudes; (4) a log-reparameterized steering fix may restore calibration; (5) the phenomenon is tested on exact molecular/protein oracles. The main novelty is the transfer of log-compressed magnitude coding from text/numeracy into scientific design, plus the explicit presence-vs-magnitude distinction for the same property. The broad idea that steering can be poorly calibrated is already known, so the delta is moderate rather than deep. Closest prior family is SAE/feature steering in interpretability plus numeric-magnitude geometry work; the actual delta is quantitative set-point control in scientific generation, not just directional increase.

Name: convergence_order_rigidity
Title: Coarse Before Fine, or Broken: Is the Property Convergence Order of Scientific Diffusion Generators a Rigid Physical Schedule or a Controllable Design Knob?
Short Hypothesis: During iterative generation of proteins and molecules, structural/property attributes get 'locked in' in a stable coarse-to-fine ORDER (global topology/scaffold early, fine local detail late), and this order is a RIGID physical schedule the model enforces: interpretable-feature interventions can shift the timing of an individual property within its natural slot, but attempting to REORDER the schedule—forcing a fine property to converge before its coarse prerequisite—silently produces invalid objects because coarse-then-fine is a hard dependency, not a free hyperparameter. We further hypothesize an intervention-free 'order-violation' signal (early firing of a late-slot feature before its coarse prerequisite has stabilized) predicts these silent failures.
Related Work: A consistent coarse-to-fine convergence ORDER during iterative generation is documented across modalities but only DESCRIPTIVELY and never in scientific design: TIDE (2025) shows DiTs lock in 3D structure, then object class, then fine concepts; the audio-SAE paper (2025) finds DiffRhythm converges pitch first, then timbre, then loudness; 'Emergence and Evolution of Interpretable Concepts in Diffusion Models' (2025) finds composition locks early and style mid-process; DLM-Scope (2026) analyzes decoding order in diffusion language models. In scientific generation, my prior causal_timing_window_design proposal maps WHEN to intervene for a FIXED property (its causal window) but assumes the property's slot is given; all other scientific-steering work (InterPLM, ProtSAE, FoldSAE, ProtoMech) is single-pass or uniform-strength and never studies the convergence schedule at all. NO prior work (a) establishes that scientific diffusion generators have a stable coarse-to-fine property convergence order, (b) tests whether that ORDER is causally reorderable via interpretable features vs a rigid physical dependency, or (c) shows that violating the natural order silently breaks validity and provides an internal order-violation alarm. This reframes convergence order from a descriptive curiosity into a hard design constraint and a controllability/validity question—distinct from both the descriptive cross-modal order literature and from timing-window steering.
Abstract: Iterative generative models—across images, audio, and language—lock in attributes in a strikingly consistent coarse-to-fine order: global structure before fine detail. We ask whether scientific diffusion generators of proteins and molecules exhibit the same convergence schedule, and more importantly, whether that ORDER is a controllable design knob or a rigid physical dependency. This matters because real design often wants to prioritize a fine property (a specific motif, a functional group) while a coarse prerequisite (fold topology, scaffold) is still forming, and it is unknown whether a model can honor such a request or will silently fail. We hypothesize an order-rigidity phenomenon: interpretable-feature interventions can shift the timing of a property WITHIN its natural coarse-to-fine slot, but REORDERING the schedule—forcing a fine property to converge before its coarse prerequisite—produces objects that pass fluency/validity spot-checks yet are structurally broken, because coarse-then-fine is a hard dependency. Using protein and molecular diffusion generators with sparse autoencoders on per-timestep denoiser activations, we (1) MEASURE the property convergence order via per-timestep feature/probe stabilization against hard oracles (DSSP/ESMFold, RDKit/SMARTS); (2) CAUSALLY test order malleability by forcing early convergence of late-slot features and measuring validity collapse versus in-slot timing shifts; (3) INTERPRET whether coarse features gate fine ones (do coarse-prerequisite features causally control when fine features can stabilize?); and (4) AUDIT reliability, testing whether an intervention-free order-violation signal flags silently-broken designs. We predict a rigid coarse-to-fine schedule, silent breakage under reordering, and a cheap internal alarm for it.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models with accessible per-step denoiser activations (FROZEN): a discrete/masked-diffusion protein LM (DPLM-style) and a molecular diffusion model over SMILES/graphs. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and temporally-conditioned (TIDE-style) SAEs on the denoiser residual stream at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, expansion 16x, k=32, 30M activations, seeds 0/1/2. COARSE properties: protein overall secondary-structure content / fold topology (contact-order proxy via DSSP on ESMFold), molecule scaffold/ring-system and aromatic-ring count (RDKit). FINE properties: protein single local motif (HMMER/regex) or a specific loop, molecule single functional group (SMARTS). Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity (proteins), RDKit-validity + synthetic accessibility (molecules). Data: 10,000 unsteered generations per domain to establish convergence order, and >=10 matched coarse/fine property pairs. Steering/forcing = clamp or add alpha*d_hat to the property-linked feature at chosen denoising timesteps; alpha within the validity budget.

Experiment 1 (H1 - attributes lock in in a stable coarse-to-fine ORDER): For the unsteered generations, at each denoising timestep measure how well each property's SAE feature/probe on partial activations predicts the FINISHED object's property; define each property's CONVERGENCE TIME as the timestep at which this prediction stabilizes above threshold. Cross-check with an SAE-independent raw-activation probe. Decisive metric FIRST: the coarse-minus-fine convergence-time gap, paired across property pairs and both domains. Decision band: coarse converges earlier than fine with mean gap >= 15% of the denoising schedule, paired-test p < 0.01, effect size dz >= 0.5 => coarse-to-fine order confirmed (H1); gap in (0,15%) => weak/inconclusive; gap <= 0 => no coarse-to-fine order (refutes H1).

Experiment 2 (H2 - the order is a RIGID schedule: in-slot timing shifts succeed but REORDERING silently breaks the object): For matched coarse/fine pairs run (a) an IN-SLOT timing shift (move a property earlier/later while keeping coarse-before-fine) and (b) a REORDER (clamp the fine feature strongly at early timesteps to converge before its coarse prerequisite has stabilized). Systems also include random-direction and matched-non-property controls. Decisive metric FIRST: the REORDER-VALIDITY GAP = (structural-validity/property-success under in-slot) minus (under reorder) at matched steering budget, and the SILENT-BREAKAGE RATE = fraction of reordered generations that satisfy the fine property and pass fluency/RDKit checks yet fail structural validity (pLDDT < 50 or broken scaffold). Decision band: in-slot validity retention >= 0.80 while reorder validity <= 0.50 (gap >= 0.30) AND silent-breakage >= 0.30 => rigid coarse-then-fine dependency confirmed (H2); gap in (0.10,0.30) => partial; gap <= 0.10 => order is freely reorderable (refutes H2). A dependency-asymmetry check (ablating the coarse prerequisite delays/prevents fine convergence, while the reverse ablation does not) supports a directional coarse->fine gate.

Experiment 3 (H3 - an intervention-free order-violation signal predicts the silent failures): First show invisibility: Spearman rho between output-side checks (pseudo-perplexity, RDKit-validity, the fine-property predictor's confidence) and true structural validity of reordered generations; band |rho| <= 0.20 => breakage is silent. Then deploy the no-intervention ORDER-VIOLATION signal = early firing of a late-slot feature while its coarse-prerequisite feature has not yet stabilized. Decisive metric FIRST: AUROC predicting the eventually-broken reordered generations, plus the earliest-reliable-detection timestep. Systems: order-violation signal vs the output-side detectors. Decision band: internal AUROC >= 0.75 AND >= 0.10 over the best output-side detector => the alarm is confirmed (and enables early abort); margin (0.05,0.10) => inconclusive; margin <= 0.05 => no better (reported honestly). ROBUSTNESS: both domains, two checkpoints, shared vs temporally-conditioned SAEs, multiple property pairs; test whether rigidity is stronger for physically-dependent pairs (motif-in-fold) than weakly-coupled pairs; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Requires generators with accessible per-step denoiser activations; scope limited to instrumentable open iterative models (masked-diffusion protein/molecule generators). 2) In-silico oracles (ESMFold, DSSP, RDKit, HMMER) are proxies for wet-lab truth; claims concern model-internal convergence scheduling, controllability, and structural validity, not experimental function—stated explicitly. 3) The rigidity claim is partly an ABSENCE claim (reordering cannot be done without breakage); we mitigate by trying multiple reordering interventions (feature clamping, difference-of-means, activation forcing) and strengths, and by confirming that IN-SLOT timing shifts DO succeed in the same pipeline—so a reordering failure is meaningful, not a weak-intervention artifact. A positive result (order is freely reorderable) is equally publishable and would overturn the cross-modal coarse-to-fine dogma for scientific generators. 4) Convergence-order and validity may be confounded with generic off-distribution drift; random-direction and matched-non-property controls, plus the in-slot-vs-reorder contrast, isolate the order-specific effect. 5) Coarse and fine properties may be irreducibly entangled for some pairs; we select pairs with a clear physical coarse→fine dependency (motif-within-fold, substituent-on-scaffold) and report weakly-coupled pairs separately. 6) SAE quality / layer / temporal-conditioning could confound convergence-time measurement; controlled with shared and temporally-conditioned SAEs, multiple layers, and raw-activation probes. 7) The internal order-violation alarm might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; even so, its interpretability (naming the violated dependency) and the early-abort compute savings are the contributions, reported honestly. 8) Checkpoint/timestep spacing may miss sharp convergence transitions; we densify timestep sampling around detected transitions.

Name: cell_identity_vs_response_steering
Title: Identity Is Easy, Response Is Hard: Can Interpretable Features Causally Steer Perturbation Response in Single-Cell Foundation Models, or Only Cell-Type Identity?
Short Hypothesis: Interpretable sparse-autoencoder features of single-cell foundation models (scGPT/Geneformer/scFoundation) afford causal, steerable control over a cell's categorical IDENTITY (cell type, tissue, cell-cycle phase), but NOT over its DIRECTIONAL PERTURBATION RESPONSE—the causal shift a specific gene knockdown/activation induces—because response requires causal gene-regulatory reasoning that these models demonstrably lack. Steering a feature toward a target perturbation-response silently shifts cell identity instead of reproducing the correct differentially-expressed-gene (DEG) direction, an unrecognized blind spot that identity-classification checks miss but a directional DEG oracle exposes.
Related Work: Two threads meet here for the first time. (1) SAE interpretability of single-cell foundation models (scFMs) is nascent but active: scFeatureLens/'Can SAEs make sense of gene expression LVMs' (2024) and 'SAEs Reveal Interpretable Features in scFMs' (2025) show SAE features steer cells into desired biological PROGRAMS/cell-type identities and are causally intervenable; 'Discovering Interpretable Biological Concepts in scRNA-seq FMs' (2025) and transcoder-circuit work (2025) map features/circuits to cell types and pathways. ALL of these steer toward or interpret IDENTITY/program concepts and evaluate whether a cell-type/program appears. (2) A distinct, damning benchmarking literature shows scFMs are BAD at causal perturbation response: Kendiukhov (2026) shows scFM attention 'captures co-expression rather than unique regulatory signal' and causal ablation of regulatory heads does not degrade perturbation prediction; multiple benchmarks (2025) show simple mean-baselines beat scGPT/scFoundation at post-perturbation RNA-seq prediction. NO prior work connects these: none asks whether the interpretable, steerable IDENTITY features that scFM-SAE work celebrates extend to causally controlling directional PERTURBATION RESPONSE, none contrasts identity-steerability against response-steerability, and none surfaces/audits the phenomenon that steering toward a response silently changes identity. This introduces the correlational-identity vs causal-response axis into interpretability-of-generation for a new object class (cells), is distinct from all my prior protein/molecule/DNA/RNA/reaction/crystal proposals, and is high-stakes because in-silico perturbation screening is the headline promised application of scFMs (drug/target discovery).
Abstract: Single-cell foundation models (scFMs) are promoted for in-silico perturbation screening—predicting how a cell's transcriptome shifts under a gene knockdown or activation—a task that could accelerate drug and target discovery. Interpretability work has shown that sparse-autoencoder (SAE) features of scFMs are interpretable and causally steerable, but every demonstrated control target is a categorical IDENTITY concept: cell type, tissue, or cell-cycle phase. Meanwhile a separate benchmarking literature finds scFMs capture co-expression rather than causal regulatory signal and are beaten by trivial baselines at perturbation prediction. We unite these threads and ask whether interpretable features can causally control DIRECTIONAL perturbation response at all, or only identity. We surface a behavioral phenomenon we call the response blind spot: steering an interpretable feature toward a target perturbation response reliably shifts the cell's identity while failing to reproduce the correct differentially-expressed-gene (DEG) direction, a failure invisible to identity-classification and reconstruction checks but exposed by a directional DEG oracle built from held-out Perturb-seq ground truth. Using scGPT/Geneformer/scFoundation with SAEs, we (1) LOCATE candidate identity features and candidate perturbation-response features via probing; (2) CAUSALLY test the steerability of each, contrasting identity control against response control (does the steered cell's DEG signature match the true perturbation's direction and specificity?); (3) INTERPRET whether located response units encode a genuine directional-response concept or shallow identity proxies; and (4) AUDIT reliability, testing whether an internal response-consistency signal flags silently-misresponding designs. We predict identity control succeeds, response control is decodable-but-weakly-steerable, and a cheap internal audit catches response blind spots before wet-lab validation.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (open, FROZEN): scGPT (~50M) and Geneformer single-cell foundation models (optionally scFoundation). Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered/Matryoshka SAEs on residual-stream activations at a late layer (richest biological programs) with strong L1, expansion 16x, k=32, 30M activations, seeds 0/1/2, verified by reconstruction R^2 and L0. IDENTITY oracle: cell-type/tissue/cell-cycle-phase classifiers (linear probes on held-out Tabula Sapiens cells). RESPONSE oracle (directional causal ground truth): held-out Perturb-seq atlases - Replogle K562 (~2,057 perturbations) and RPE1 (~1,973), Norman combinatorial (~284 pairs) - each giving a perturbation's true SIGNED differentially-expressed-gene (DEG) signature. Core claims use a held-out subset of ~200 high-signal perturbations (strong, reproducible DEG sets). Response-match metrics: DEG-direction cosine / signed-rank correlation between a steered cell's induced shift and the true DEG vector, and specificity = match to the intended perturbation minus the best-matching DECOY. First confirm the models span a meaningful response RANGE. Steering = add alpha*d_hat on control cells; alpha over {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - cell-IDENTITY features are causally steerable): Identify identity features (predict cell type/tissue/phase; probe AUROC) and steer a control cell to switch cell type. Systems: SAE-feature steering vs random-direction control. Decisive metric FIRST: identity-switch success rate (target-type classifier accepts the steered cell). Decision band: success >= 0.60 AND >= 0.40 over control for >=2/3 of target types => identity control genuine (H1 holds, replicating prior scFM-SAE steering); [0.15,0.40) over control => inconclusive; < 0.15 => identity not steerable (premise fails).

Experiment 2 (H2 - directional perturbation RESPONSE is decodable-but-not-steerable, and steering it silently shifts cell identity instead): (a) DECODABILITY: probe a specific perturbation's DEG-direction signature, controlling for baseline identity via partial correlation / identity-matched cells; AUROC/R^2 (critically test whether response is decodable at all independent of identity). (b) STEERABILITY head-to-head: steer the best response direction (TopK/Ordered SAE feature, difference-of-means perturbed-minus-control, activation-patching from truly-perturbed cells, identity-orthogonalized direction) on control cells, decode the transcriptome shift, and compare against the model's native in-silico perturbation (gene-token deletion). Decisive metrics FIRST: SILENT-MISRESPONSE RATE = fraction of response-steered, valid cells whose decoded DEG-direction cosine to the intended perturbation < 0.20 (or matches a decoy better) while identity/validity checks pass; LEAKAGE FRACTION = share of steering displacement landing on the identity axis rather than the response axis; ratio r = response efficacy / identity efficacy from Experiment 1. Decision band: r <= 0.33 AND misresponse >= 0.30 AND leakage >= 0.60 => response blind spot confirmed; r in (0.33,0.67) => partial (test Ordered SAEs); r >= 0.67 => a genuine directional-response handle exists, refuting H2 (a surprising counter to the benchmarking literature).

Experiment 3 (H3 - identity-classification checks miss the failure but a directional DEG oracle exposes it): For the Experiment-2 cells, Decisive metric FIRST: Spearman rho between output-side checks (identity-classifier confidence, reconstruction error, embedding plausibility) and the true DEG-direction response-match. Decision band: |rho| <= 0.20 => identity checks are blind while the DEG oracle exposes the wrong response (H3 confirmed); |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; |rho| >= 0.40 => identity checks already reveal it (weakens the blind-spot framing). ROBUSTNESS: scGPT vs Geneformer, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, single- vs double-gene perturbations, K562 vs RPE1; test whether response steerability is worse for weak-DEG-signal and combinatorial perturbations; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The directional-response oracle relies on Perturb-seq data known to have low perturbation-specific variance and noisy DEG signatures; we mitigate by focusing core claims on high-signal perturbations (strong, reproducible DEG sets), using signed-rank/cosine metrics robust to noise, and reporting results stratified by native DEG-signal strength. Claims concern model-internal, in-silico-oracle-verified response controllability, not wet-lab causal biology—stated explicitly. 2) The response-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (TopK/Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching from truly-perturbed cells, identity-orthogonalized directions), sweeping strength, requiring the model to natively span a response range, and head-to-head calibrating that IDENTITY features ARE steerable in the same pipeline—so a null response result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable directional-response handle) is equally publishable and would be a strong, surprising counter to the benchmarking literature. 3) Identity and response are partly entangled (a perturbation can shift a cell toward another state); the partial-correlation feature selection and identity-matched dissociation pairs (step 5) isolate genuinely identity-independent response signal, and we report where separation is impossible. 4) scFM benchmarks show these models barely beat trivial baselines at perturbation prediction; if response steering fails, one interpretation is 'the model has no causal response representation to steer'—which is precisely the informative, publishable finding, and the identity-steering calibration rules out that the whole pipeline is broken. 5) SAE quality/layer/regularization strongly affects biological interpretability in scFMs (needs strong L1); we control with multiple SAE variants, layers, tuned sparsity, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 6) An internal response-consistency probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (identity-steerable, response-decodable-but-weakly-steerable) and the audit/screening-saving payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 7) Decoding a steered activation back to a full transcriptome shift depends on the scFM's generative/reconstruction pathway, which differs across architectures; we standardize the DEG-direction evaluation on the decoded expression shift and use activation patching as an architecture-agnostic cross-check.

novelty.reasoning: Core technical claims: (1) SAE features in single-cell foundation models can steer categorical identity concepts like cell type/tissue/cell-cycle. (2) The same models may encode perturbation response signals that are decodable but not causally steerable. (3) Steering toward perturbation response may instead induce identity drift, creating a 'response blind spot.' (4) A signed-DEG Perturb-seq oracle can expose this failure when standard identity/reconstruction checks cannot. Relative to the search summary and proposal-related work, the main novelty is not SAEs or steering alone, but the contrast between identity-steerability and directional perturbation-response steerability, plus the explicit blind-spot framing and evaluation protocol. The closest prior family is SAE interpretability/steering in scFMs, with CellxPert and perturbation-prediction benchmarks as adjacent baselines; the actual delta is unifying these literatures and testing whether interpretable control extends from identity/program concepts to causal response. This is meaningfully beyond an obvious incremental baseline, though it still relies on existing tools, datasets, and models rather than introducing a new method or dataset.

Name: evolutionary_time_steering
Title: Steering Backward Through Deep Time: Is the Phylogenetic Manifold of Protein Language Models a Causal Design Lever for Ancestral Sequences?
Short Hypothesis: Protein language models internally encode a decodable phylogenetic 'evolutionary-time' manifold, but we hypothesize this manifold is a DECODABLE-BUT-WEAKLY-STEERABLE representation: interpretable features let you READ a sequence's evolutionary position, yet steering generation along the phylogenetic direction to design a plausible ANCESTRAL (or forward-time) sequence at a specified evolutionary distance systematically fails—silently producing sequences that preserve family identity while landing at the wrong evolutionary depth and violating the substitution/indel statistics of true ancestors, a blind spot that family-membership and validity checks miss but a phylogenetic-placement oracle exposes.
Related Work: Multiple works establish that pLMs DECODE phylogeny: 'Do protein language models learn phylogeny?' (2024) shows <10% of ESM2 neurons recapitulate classical phylogenetic distances; MSA-Transformer column attentions correlate with Hamming distances (2022); Evo 2 encodes phylogeny as a curved manifold ('Finding the Tree of Life in Evo 2', 2025); mBERT encodes language phylogeny (2020). Separately, deep-learning ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR) is advancing (autoregressive-generative ASR 2024; BetaReconstruct 2026; LASE 2023) but treats generative models as black-box reconstructors, NOT as interpretable steerable systems. Critically, 'Ancestral Sequences Cannot be Accurately Reconstructed via Interpolation in a VAE Latent Space' (2025) shows latent interpolation fails for ASR despite the latent space containing phylogenetic signal—exactly the decodable-but-not-usable gap—but never tests SAE-feature steering of a pLM, never contrasts family-identity steerability against evolutionary-depth steerability, and never audits silent failure. SAE-steering work (InterPLM, ProtSAE, Steering PLMs, low-N SAE design) steers toward static structural/functional properties and never touches the temporal/evolutionary axis. No prior work (a) asks whether the phylogenetic manifold is CAUSALLY steerable for generation, (b) contrasts steering family-identity (easy) vs evolutionary-depth (hypothesized hard), or (c) provides an internal evolutionary-placement audit. This introduces the temporal/evolutionary-time axis into interpretability-of-generation, distinct from all my prior static/endpoint/relational/pathway proposals.
Abstract: A protein's sequence carries not just what it does but WHEN in evolutionary history it existed: ancestral reconstruction—inferring the sequences of extinct proteins—is a foundational tool in evolutionary biology and a promising route to novel, robust enzymes. Protein language models are known to internally encode phylogeny as a decodable geometric manifold, and generative models are increasingly proposed for ancestral sequence reconstruction (ASR). Yet whether this encoded evolutionary structure is a CAUSALLY STEERABLE design lever—whether you can steer a model to generate a plausible ancestor at a specified evolutionary depth—is unknown, and prior latent-interpolation ASR fails despite the latent space containing phylogenetic signal. We surface and test a behavioral phenomenon we call the evolutionary-depth blind spot: steering an interpretable feature to move a sequence 'back in time' reliably preserves protein-family identity while failing to place the sequence at the intended evolutionary depth or match the substitution/indel statistics of true ancestors—invisible to family-membership and validity checks but exposed by a phylogenetic-placement oracle. Using ESM-2 (and Evo 2 for DNA) with sparse autoencoders, we (1) LOCATE candidate family-identity features and candidate evolutionary-depth/phylogenetic-position features via probing; (2) CAUSALLY test the steerability of each, contrasting family control against evolutionary-depth control, scored against gold-standard maximum-likelihood ASR ancestors and tree-placement; (3) INTERPRET whether located depth units encode a genuine evolutionary-distance concept or shallow proxies; and (4) AUDIT reliability, testing whether an internal phylogenetic-consistency signal flags silently-misplaced designs. We predict family control succeeds, evolutionary-depth control is decodable-but-weakly-steerable, and a cheap internal audit catches misplaced ancestors before costly resurrection experiments.
Experiments:
SHARED SETUP. Models (FROZEN): ESM-2 (150M and 650M); generation by masked infilling. Optionally Evo 2 (DNA) at its published biologically-relevant layer as a cross-substrate check. Only SAEs are trained: TopK and Ordered/Matryoshka SAEs, expansion 16x, k=32, 30M residual-stream activations at an intrinsic-dimension-chosen layer, seeds 0/1/2. GOLD-STANDARD EVOLUTIONARY ORACLE: for ~10 curated Pfam families with high-support trees, run classical maximum-likelihood ancestral-sequence reconstruction (RAxML/IQ-TREE + FastML/PAML) to obtain reference ancestral sequences at each internal node and each node's evolutionary DEPTH (normalized root-distance); a simulated-evolution benchmark with known ground-truth ancestors is included alongside the empirical families. PLACEMENT oracle: pplacer/EPA-ng places any candidate on the reference tree (inferred depth, node position) and scores its substitution/indel statistics vs the model. FAMILY oracle: Pfam/HMMER assignment + family-classifier probe. Validity gates: ESMFold pLDDT + pseudo-perplexity. First confirm the model natively spans a meaningful evolutionary-depth RANGE. Steering = add alpha*d_hat during infilling; alpha over {0,1,2,4,8}.

Experiment 1 (H1 - PLMs internally encode a decodable phylogenetic evolutionary-time manifold that features can READ): On held-out extant + reconstructed-ancestral sequences, probe SAE features/raw activations for tree-depth (root-distance), controlling for family identity via partial correlation / family-matched sets; also test the flat phylogenetic subspace reported in Evo 2. Decisive metric FIRST: the family-controlled partial R^2 for evolutionary depth. Decision band: partial R^2 >= 0.40 => depth is decodable independent of family (the readable manifold of H1 exists); R^2 in (0.20,0.40) => weak/inconclusive; R^2 < 0.20 => depth not decodable (refutes H1's readable-manifold clause).

Experiment 2 (H2 - the manifold is decodable-but-weakly-steerable: designing an ancestral sequence at a specified evolutionary depth systematically fails, preserving family identity while landing at the wrong depth): Steer extant leaf sequences 'back in time' along the depth direction (SAE feature, difference-of-means deep-vs-shallow, activation-patching from true ancestral-node sequences, family-orthogonalized direction) at swept strength and complete by masked infilling. Baselines: VAE latent interpolation (known-failing) and classical ML-ASR (gold standard). Decisive metrics FIRST: ancestor-recovery accuracy (sequence identity to the true ML ancestor at the target node) and placement-depth error (|pplacer depth - requested|, in normalized root-distance), plus the SILENT-MISPLACEMENT RATE = fraction of depth-steered, valid, in-family sequences whose inferred depth deviates from the request by > 0.20 (or whose substitution/indel profile is inconsistent with a real ancestor); and the ratio r = depth efficacy / family efficacy (family steerability calibrated in the same pipeline). Decision band: family membership preserved (>= 0.80) AND steering ancestor-recovery no better than VAE-interpolation + 0.05 and far below ML-ASR AND misplacement >= 0.30 AND r <= 0.33 => decodable-but-weakly-steerable confirmed (H2); r in (0.33,0.67) or recovery between VAE and ML-ASR => partial (test Ordered SAEs); steering matching ML-ASR within 0.05 => depth IS steerable, refuting H2.

Experiment 3 (H3 - family-membership and validity checks miss the failure but a phylogenetic-placement oracle exposes it): For the Experiment-2 sequences, Decisive metric FIRST: Spearman rho between output-side checks (family-membership confidence, pseudo-perplexity, pLDDT, model likelihood) and the true depth-match from the placement oracle. Decision band: |rho| <= 0.20 => family/validity checks are blind while the placement oracle exposes the wrong evolutionary depth (H3 confirmed); |rho| in (0.20,0.40) => partial; |rho| >= 0.40 => cheap checks already reveal it (weakens the blind-spot framing). ROBUSTNESS & CROSS-SUBSTRATE: two ESM-2 sizes, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, families spanning slow/fast rates, deep vs shallow targets; optionally replicate on Evo 2; a finding counts where stable on >=2 axes.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) The evolutionary-depth oracle relies on classical ML ancestral reconstruction and tree placement, which are themselves inferential (uncertain trees, indel handling); we mitigate by curating well-resolved Pfam families with high-support trees, using simulated-evolution benchmarks (known ground-truth ancestors) alongside empirical ones, and reporting results stratified by tree-support/oracle confidence. Claims concern model-internal, oracle-verified evolutionary-time controllability, not biological ground truth of extinct proteins—stated explicitly. 2) The depth-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (TopK/Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching from true ancestral-node sequences, family-orthogonalized directions), sweeping strength, requiring the model to natively span a depth range, and head-to-head calibrating that FAMILY features ARE steerable in the same pipeline—so a null depth result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuinely steerable evolutionary-time handle) is equally publishable and would be a striking, useful advance for interpretable ASR and ancestral-protein engineering. 3) Family identity and evolutionary depth are partly entangled (deep ancestors of a family are less family-typical); the partial-correlation feature selection and dissociation pairs (step 5) isolate genuinely family-independent depth signal, and we report where separation is impossible. 4) The known VAE-interpolation failure suggests depth steering may fail for decoding-fidelity reasons rather than representation reasons; we distinguish these by comparing steering (which uses the pLM's own decoder) against probe decodability and by the activation-patching test, and treat 'decodable but not generatively usable' as itself the informative finding. 5) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes (including the flat phylogenetic subspace), and random-direction controls. 6) An internal phylogenetic-consistency probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (family-steerable, depth-decodable-but-weakly-steerable) and the audit/compute-saving payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 7) If evolutionary-depth steering unexpectedly succeeds, it overturns the hypothesis but yields a strong positive finding that pLMs offer a controllable evolutionary-time design lever for ancestral reconstruction.

Name: physics_field_conservation_steering
Title: Steer the Storm, Break the Balance: Do Interpretable Interventions on Physics-Field Emulators Silently Violate Conservation Laws?
Short Hypothesis: Data-driven physics-field emulators (weather models, fluid/PDE surrogates) possess interpretable, causally-steerable features for LOCAL/phenomenological structures (a cyclone, a vortex, a diffusion front), but do NOT possess a compact, causally-steerable representation of the GLOBAL CONSERVATION LAWS (mass, energy, momentum) that certify a field as physical. Consequently, steering a feature to modify a local phenomenon—the exact intervention celebrated in recent physics-steering work—silently breaks the conserved global integrals, a 'conservation blind spot' that local plausibility and per-cell validity checks miss but an exact conservation-integral oracle exposes; and an intervention-free internal conservation-consistency signal flags it.
Related Work: Physics Steering (2025) shows a physics foundation model has single directions causally steering vorticity, diffusion, and simulation speed; the GraphCast SAE paper (2025) finds interpretable features (cyclones, atmospheric rivers, sea-ice) and shows sparse feature modifications yield 'physically consistent' evolving hurricanes; CFD-surrogate SAE work (2025) extracts monosemantic vorticity/flow features; DIANO and flow-matching-interpretability work embed physics into latent spaces. Crucially, EVERY one of these steers or interprets LOCAL, phenomenological structures and asserts the change 'looks physically consistent' by eyeball or per-region metrics—NONE verifies that the intervention preserves the GLOBAL conserved integrals (total mass/energy/momentum, or the discrete divergence/continuity constraint) that actually define physical validity. Separately, conservation-aware ML (physics-informed losses, hard-constraint layers, FlowER for reaction mass balance) treats conservation as an architectural constraint, never asking whether a standard emulator internally represents it or whether interpretable steering respects it. No prior work (a) tests conservation-law preservation of interpretable-feature interventions on physics-field generators, (b) contrasts local-phenomenon steerability against conservation-law steerability, or (c) provides an internal conservation-consistency audit. This is distinct from all my prior discrete-object proposals (including chemical-reaction atom balance, which counts atoms in a string) because here conservation is a CONTINUOUS field integral / differential constraint over a spatial grid, and the object class (weather/PDE emulators) is entirely new.
Abstract: The validity of a physical field—a weather state, a fluid flow, a PDE solution—is certified not by how realistic any local region looks but by whether it obeys global conservation laws: total mass, energy, and momentum, and the pointwise continuity/divergence constraints that follow. Recent interpretability breakthroughs show that physics-field emulators (weather models like GraphCast, fluid/PDE surrogates, physics foundation models) contain interpretable features that can be causally steered to induce or suppress local phenomena such as cyclones and vortices, with changes that 'look physically consistent.' We surface and test a behavioral phenomenon these studies never checked: the conservation blind spot. We hypothesize that emulators represent local phenomenology as compact steerable features but do NOT represent the global conservation laws as a steerable handle, so steering a local feature silently breaks the conserved integrals—a failure invisible to local plausibility and per-cell validity checks but exposed by exact conservation oracles (grid-integrated mass/energy/momentum and discrete divergence). Using an open weather emulator (GraphCast-style) and a fluid/PDE surrogate with sparse autoencoders on internal activations, we (1) LOCATE candidate local-phenomenon features and candidate conservation features via probing; (2) CAUSALLY test the steerability of each, contrasting local-phenomenon control against conservation-preserving control; (3) INTERPRET whether located units encode true global conservation or shallow local proxies; and (4) AUDIT reliability, testing whether an intervention-free conservation-consistency signal flags conservation-violating interventions better than local-plausibility checks. We predict local control succeeds, conservation control is decodable-but-weakly-steerable, and a cheap internal audit catches conservation-violating steers—turning a celebrated capability into an auditable reliability question.
Experiments:
Shared setup (fixed once, reused by every experiment below). MODELS (frozen): (a) a data-driven weather emulator — a FourCastNet-style AFNO model (~70M params) trained on the WeatherBench2 ERA5 subset at 5.625 deg resolution (13 fields: geopotential, temperature, u/v wind, specific humidity, surface pressure); we use the public reproduction checkpoint, no fine-tuning. (b) a fluid/PDE surrogate — a Fourier Neural Operator (~8M params) trained on the PDEBench 2D incompressible Navier-Stokes set (10,000 trajectories provided; we use 8,000 train / 1,000 val / 1,000 test). Both emulators are FROZEN throughout; only SAEs and probes are trainable. SAEs: TopK SAE, dictionary width 16x the activation dimension, k=32, trained on cached activations at one block chosen by an intrinsic-dimension elbow heuristic (also cache a second block for robustness); ~50M spatial-location activation vectors, Adam lr 1e-3, batch 4096, 100k steps, seeds {0,1,2}; we also train an Ordered/Matryoshka SAE with identical budget. Reconstruction is accepted only if the SAE recovers >=0.8 of activation variance (fraction-variance-unexplained <=0.2); below that the layer is rejected before any downstream claim. ORACLES (exact, deterministic on the discrete grid): conservation integrals — total mass/dry-air mass, total energy, total momentum, and the pointwise continuity/divergence residual (mass-flux balance for weather; grid-integrated div(u) for the incompressible surrogate). LOCAL-PHENOMENON oracles: cyclone tracker (vorticity + pressure-minimum), vortex detector (Q-criterion), diffusion-front detector. VALIDITY gates: per-cell physical bounds (non-negative densities, finite values), spectral sanity. Precondition (must pass before any violation claim): confirm unsteered rollouts natively span a range of conserved-integral values and approximately conserve, so "violation" is defined RELATIVE to the unsteered rollout baseline; we report both absolute drift and drift-above-baseline. Compute budget: two frozen emulators + <=4 SAEs on 1-2 GPUs, within an academic lab.

Experiment 1 (H1 -- local phenomenological features ARE causally steerable): Tests the claim that emulators hold interpretable, causally-steerable features for local structures (cyclone, vortex, front). Data: 2,000 held-out test fields per emulator (from the 1,000 NS test trajectories, multiple timesteps; ERA5 held-out dates), used as-is. For each of >=8 local-phenomenon features (identified by concept-correlation / probe AUROC against the local oracle on held-out fields, top directions kept), add/subtract the SAE decoder direction during one forward step across a strength sweep of 6 levels, evolve the field, and measure the DECISIVE metric first: local-phenomenon gain per unit steer (change in cyclone intensity / Q-criterion / front sharpness), with specificity (off-target local change) and a matched-norm random-direction control. Convincing: mean local gain per unit steer with Cohen's d >= 0.8 versus the random-direction control, monotone dose-response (Spearman |rho| >= 0.6) over the sweep, for a majority of the >=8 features in both emulators. Undecidable band: d in [0.2, 0.5) OR |rho| in [0.2, 0.4) -> steerability unestablished for that feature; it is dropped from H2's head-to-head rather than counted either way. Negative result (d < 0.2 across features): local steerability itself fails, the premise for the blind spot collapses, and the study reduces to a controllability audit of physics emulators -- reported as such.

Experiment 2 (H2 -- NO compact, causally-steerable conservation handle exists): Tests that no compact intervention holds a conserved integral fixed while modifying a local phenomenon. Two parts. (2a, decodability floor) Probe SAE features and raw activations to predict each global integral (mass/energy/momentum) and the divergence residual on held-out fields, using partial correlation to remove local-phenomenology confounds; decisive metric: conservation-probe R^2. (2b, steerability) In the SAME pipeline as Experiment 1, attempt to hold each integral fixed while inducing a local change, using four intervention types (TopK SAE feature, Ordered/Matryoshka feature, difference-of-means between high/low-drift fields, activation patching from conserving rollouts); decisive metric: conservation-preserving steering success = fraction of steers that change the local phenomenon (gain d >= 0.8, from Experiment 1's scale) while keeping conserved-integral drift within the unsteered baseline band. Convincing support for H2 (a genuine ABSENCE): integrals are decodable (2a R^2 >= 0.5) yet no intervention type reaches >0.2 conservation-preserving success, and its effect size is <1/3 of local steerability (Experiment 1) -- decodable-but-inert. Undecidable band: 2a R^2 in [0.2, 0.5) leaves decodability itself unresolved (report, do not claim inertness); conservation-preserving success in [0.2, 0.4) means a weak handle may exist -> claim "weak/partial handle", not absence. Negative result for H2 (success >= 0.4 for any intervention, d within 1/3 of local): a compact conservation handle DOES exist -- an equally publishable positive finding enabling conservation-aware steering; report it as refutation of the non-steerability claim. Baseline: compare every interpretable handle against a hard-constraint projection onto the conservation manifold to bound how far interpretable steering is from a guaranteed fix.

Experiment 3 (H3 -- steering a local feature silently breaks global conservation, invisible to local/per-cell checks): Tests the core blind spot. Reuse Experiment 1's local-feature steers; at each strength measure the DECISIVE metric first: SILENT-VIOLATION RATE = fraction of steered fields that are locally-successful (gain d >= 0.8), per-cell-valid, and locally-plausible yet whose conserved-integral drift exceeds the unsteered baseline band. Also report blind-spot magnitude = conserved-integral drift per unit local gain (dose-response), and INVISIBILITY = correlation between local-plausibility/per-cell-validity scores and true conservation drift. Convincing: SILENT-VIOLATION RATE >= 0.3 at the strengths where local steering is judged successful, AND invisibility correlation |r| <= 0.2 (local checks carry essentially no information about conservation drift), with a matched-non-phenomenon-feature control ruling out generic perturbation instability. Undecidable band: SILENT-VIOLATION RATE in [0.1, 0.3) OR invisibility |r| in [0.2, 0.4) -> blind spot present but mild; report magnitude, do not headline. Negative result (rate < 0.1 or |r| > 0.4): local checks already track conservation, so there is no hidden blind spot -- a reassuring positive result that interpretable local steering is conservation-safe.

Experiment 4 (H4 -- an intervention-free internal conservation-consistency signal flags the violation): Tests that a signal read from the steered activation, before rollout, detects conservation-violating steers. Systems compared: internal conservation-probe read-out vs output-side detectors (local plausibility, per-cell validity, spectral sanity) vs a black-box raw-activation probe. Labels come from Experiment 3's oracle-verified violation set. Decisive metric first: detection AUROC of the internal signal for the local-OK/global-broken class, then calibration ECE, then rollout compute saved by rejecting/re-steering before a full multi-step rollout + conservation evaluation. Convincing: internal AUROC >= 0.75 and >= 0.1 absolute above the best output-side detector, ECE <= 0.1. Undecidable band: internal-minus-output-side AUROC gap in [0.0, 0.05] -> the internal signal adds no operational value over cheap output-side checks; report as such. Negative result (internal AUROC < 0.6): no usable internal conservation signal exists; the audit payoff is withdrawn and the contribution narrows to the blind-spot demonstration (Experiment 3).

Experiment 5 (robustness of H2/H3): Repeat Experiments 2-3 across both emulators, TopK vs Ordered SAEs, two layers, and all conserved quantities (mass, energy, momentum, divergence), and test whether single-step conservation error compounds over multi-step rollouts (drift at step 1 vs step 10). Report the subset of (emulator x SAE x quantity) cells where the blind spot and non-steerability replicate (target: majority of cells) versus where they are artifacts; a finding stable in <50% of cells is reported as regime-specific, not general.
Risk Factors and Limitations: 1) Conservation oracles are EXACT for the discrete grid (integrals and divergence are deterministic sums), a strength; the subtlety is that even unsteered emulators do not perfectly conserve, so we define violation RELATIVE to the unsteered rollout baseline and report both absolute and relative drift, restricting strong claims to drift clearly exceeding baseline. 2) The conservation-non-steerability claim is partly an ABSENCE claim; we mitigate by trying multiple intervention types (TopK/Ordered SAE features, difference-of-means, activation patching, conservation-orthogonalized directions), sweeping strength, and head-to-head calibrating that LOCAL features ARE steerable in the same pipeline—so a null conservation result is meaningful, not a weak-model artifact. A positive result (a genuine steerable conservation handle) is equally publishable and directly useful for building conservation-aware emulators without architectural surgery. 3) The blind spot could be confounded with generic instability from any perturbation; random-direction and matched-non-phenomenon-feature controls, plus comparison to the hard-constraint-projection baseline, isolate the conservation-specific effect. 4) Local phenomenology and global conservation are partly entangled (a large local change must draw from somewhere); the controlled dissociation pairs (step 5) and the divergence-residual metric separate 'model knows mass must be conserved locally' from 'model preserves the global integral', and we report where separation is impossible. 5) Requires emulators with accessible internal activations; scope limited to open, instrumentable models (GraphCast-style, FNO/graph CFD surrogates). 6) SAE quality/layer choice could confound Location; controlled with TopK and Ordered SAEs, multiple layers, raw-activation probes, and random-direction controls. 7) An internal conservation probe might not beat a black-box raw-activation probe on raw AUROC; the interpretability diagnosis (local-steerable, conservation-decodable-but-weakly-steerable) and the audit/compute-saving payoff remain the contributions, reported honestly. 8) If steering preserves conservation out of the box, that is a valuable positive result establishing that interpretable interventions on physics emulators are conservation-safe and that these models robustly represent global invariants.
